events.text: The barrier closes behind you with a sound like a tent flap in wind. {sr_realm} runs to the edge of sight: rust-red grass, broken chariots half sunk in it, and arrowheads pushing up through the soil like mushrooms after rain. Somewhere under the ground, slow and patient, a war drum is beating.

choices.text: Pull one arrowhead out of the earth

effects.log: It comes up warm, as if it had just been loosed. You keep it, and it never cools.

choices.text: Bow to the field before you take a step

effects.log: You bow to nine hundred years of the dead. The drum under your feet misses a beat, then goes on.

choices.text: Walk in without stopping

effects.log: You walk fast and do not look down. Your legs learn the broken ground long before your eyes do.

events.text: Dusk comes early here. As the light goes, shapes stand up out of the grass all across the plain: soldiers in old lamellar, banners without colour, horses with nothing inside their ribs but mist. None of them looks at you. They are forming lines, facing a ford that has been dry for nine centuries.

choices.text: Watch them form up and learn the order of their lines

effects.log: By full dark you know where the spearmen stand and where the gaps are. It is a soldier's lesson, and it costs only nerve.

choices.text: Find a hollow and sleep through the night

effects.log: You sleep badly, to the sound of a battle that never ends, and wake rested anyway. The dead leave alone anyone who keeps out of their way.

choices.text: Walk among the lines while they are still forming

ok.log: A ghost captain looks straight through you and moves a soldier aside so you can pass. You come out the far side shaking, and a little famous among the parties who watched.

fail.log: A spear butt you never saw knocks you flat. Ghosts, it turns out, still mind their formation.

events.text: The party from {sr_sect} pitches its tents on a low rise with a view of the ford. The senior disciple in charge hands out the orders: stay in sight of the banner, touch nothing that hums, and come back by the third dusk. Then quietly, to you alone: "The elders want the spear art. If you see a chance, they will remember who took it."

choices.text: Promise to bring it home for the sect

effects.log: The senior disciple nods once. Your name is on someone's list now, for better or worse.

choices.text: Say you will bring yourself home first

effects.log: A short laugh. "Honest, at least." The orders for you are a little looser after that.

choices.text: Ask who came back from the last opening

effects.log: Nobody in the party knows. Sixty years is a long time, and the sect's records of it are thin. That alone is a warning.

events.text: The crack in the barrier opens beside a collapsed watchtower. On top of it, a ghost sentry still keeps the watch, calling the hours to a camp that is not there. When you climb out of the crack, he turns and calls down: "Password!"

choices.text: Answer "Dallae", the only word on the plain you know

effects.log: The sentry hesitates, then waves you through. It was the right word, or near enough.

choices.text: Say nothing and keep low

effects.log: He calls the challenge twice more, then goes back to the hours. You slip past under his voice.

choices.text: Salute him like a soldier coming off duty

effects.log: He salutes back, slow and stiff. For a breath he looks less lonely.

events.text: Nothing the old stories told you prepared you for the smell: wet iron and crushed grass, as if the battle ended an hour ago and nine hundred years at once. This is your first time inside a great realm. Everyone around you is pretending they are not afraid, and doing it badly.

choices.text: Admit to yourself that you are afraid, and go on

effects.log: Naming it makes it smaller. Your hands stop shaking before the others' do.

choices.text: Pretend better than the others

effects.log: Two juniors start to follow your lead. It is a burden, and a little fame.

choices.text: Write the date in the dirt, in case you never leave

effects.log: You write it, and your name, and feel foolish. Later you will be glad of it.

events.text: You know this hill. You have never seen it in this life, but your feet go up the left side, where the ground is firmer, before you think about it. At the top a rusted spear stands upright in the earth, the haft wrapped in cord the way you would wrap it. Some other life of yours left it here, and it waited.

choices.text: Pull the spear out and hold it

effects.log: The balance is right in your hands, the way an old shoe is right on the foot. You leave it standing, but the grip stays in your palm.

choices.text: Leave it where it stands, a marker for the next life

effects.log: You retie the cord where it has rotted. Whoever you are next time will know the way.

choices.text: Sit by it and try to remember more

effects.log: Pieces come: a campfire, someone laughing, a cold dawn. Not a whole life, but enough to know it was lived.

events.text: A ghost soldier steps out of the grass in front of you and stops. He looks at your face for a long time, then touches his fist to his chest: the salute the dead of this field give each other. He has seen you before. Behind him, on the slope, is a small cairn of stones that some past life of yours never left.

choices.text: Return the salute

effects.log: He nods, satisfied, and walks back into the grass. The dead of this plain count you as one of theirs. It is not a comfort, but it is a kind of safety.

choices.text: Go to the cairn and add a stone

effects.log: One stone for the life that ended here. The drum under the earth beats softer for a while.

choices.text: Turn your back on the cairn

effects.log: You do not owe that life a visit. The soldier watches you go with something like pity.

events.text: Realm after realm, opening after opening: you have walked into enough cracks in the world to read them like a map. This one has the oldest smell of any. The juniors at the gate are arguing about which way to go. You already know which way the wind comes from and where the ground will be soft.

choices.text: Tell them the way, plainly

effects.log: They take it, and three of them may live because of it. Your name goes around the camp that night.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself and go first

effects.log: You are halfway across the first ridge before they finish arguing.

choices.text: Teach the youngest one how to read a realm

effects.log: It takes an hour you could have spent walking. The child listens as if it were scripture.

events.text: At the gate the young elites of a dozen sects stare at the grey in your hair. A few of them whisper; one, braver, asks if you are lost. Your knees ache in the cold of the realm. They also remember sixty more years of fighting than any of these children have lived.

choices.text: Tell the child you were fighting before the child's master was born

effects.log: A ripple of laughter, then a wider path for you. Age is armour too.

choices.text: Say nothing and walk in ahead of all of them

effects.log: The whispers stop when they see how you move.

choices.text: Admit your knees hurt, and ask for a hand up the bank

effects.log: The braver one gives it. You learn the name and remember it.

events.text: The drum under the earth is not loud, but each beat presses on your chest like a hand. The others seem able to bear it. You are not; your qi is too thin for this place, and the realm knows it. The guardian of this field is far beyond anything you have ever stood against.

choices.text: Breathe with the drum instead of against it

effects.log: It takes half the day to find the rhythm. When you do, the weight eases, and something in your channels widens.

choices.text: Stay near the strongest party and keep your head down

effects.log: Nobody notices you, which is the point.

choices.text: Turn the fear into a vow: you will come out alive

effects.log: A vow made at the edge of a great realm has weight. You feel it settle in your spine.

events.text: Across the plain, on the next rise, a banner goes up over a small camp, and you know whose it is before you can read it. Your rival came in too. Of course your rival came in. Whatever lies at the end of this field, it will not be won without a race.

choices.text: Raise your own banner where it can be seen

effects.log: An answer comes back across the plain: a horn, short and mocking. The race is on.

choices.text: Move off at once, before your rival is ready

effects.log: You are a ridge ahead by the time the other camp stirs.

choices.text: Watch the other camp for an hour and learn its habits

effects.log: You learn who stands guard and who sleeps. It will be useful.

events.arc: The Boy with the Ninth Banner
events.text: A boy in armour too big for him comes running through the grass, a war banner taller than he is held up in both hands. His face is grey; his feet make no sound. "Are you from Dallae?" he gasps. "Did the city get out? I have a letter for my mother. The general said I could send it when the boats were away." His name, he says, is Ok-bin.

choices.text: Promise to carry his letter

effects.log: He presses a folded square of paper into your hand. It weighs nothing at all, and you put it next to your heart.

choices.text: Tell him gently that the city is nine hundred years gone

effects.log: He stands very still. "Then it got out," he says at last. "Then we held." He does not cry. Ghosts may not be able to.

choices.text: Tell him you have no time for ghosts

effects.log: He lowers the banner and walks back into the grass. You do not see him again, and you look for him more than once.

events.text: At the edge of the field a young spearman in crimson is already practising, alone, his lance moving through the forms of the Red Lance Hall faster than you can follow. Hyeon Mu-gyeol: the hall's prodigy, said to be the best spear of his generation. He stops when he sees you. "You want the general's art too. Truce until the guardian, or a race from here?"

choices.text: Truce until the guardian

effects.log: He clasps your forearm, hard. "Until the guardian," he repeats, and you both know what that means after.

choices.text: A race, then

effects.log: He grins, and is gone into the grass before you have finished saying it.

choices.text: Tell him the art will choose for itself

effects.log: He looks at you as if you had said something in a foreign tongue. "Arts do not choose. People take." He walks off. You have made an enemy, or a lesson.

events.text: There is smoke where there should be none: a cook fire in a trench, and an old woman stirring a pot of grass soup. Her robes are of a sect that closed its doors before you were born. "Is it the opening already?" she asks. "I was nineteen at the last one. I missed the gate." Her name is Gu Bok-rye. Sixty scratches mark the shield beside her, one for every year.

choices.text: Promise to take her out when the gate opens

effects.log: She does not believe you, and thanks you anyway, and gives you the best bowl of soup.

choices.text: Ask her for everything she knows about the field

effects.log: She talks for an hour: the soft ground, the cavalry's path, where the general stands. Sixty years of knowledge, for one bowl of company.

choices.text: Leave her to her fire

effects.log: She nods as if she expected nothing else. When you look back she is adding a stick to the fire, very carefully.

events.text: Halfway across the plain the road passes a fallen standard, its pole snapped, the silk faded to the colour of dust. A dozen ghost soldiers sit around it in a ring, not moving, as if waiting for someone to pick it up and tell them where to go.

choices.text: Stand the standard back up

effects.log: The ring of soldiers rises, salutes the pole, and marches off toward the ford. The road ahead is a little clearer.

choices.text: Walk around them

effects.log: They never look up. Some waits are not yours to end.

choices.text: Cut a strip from the silk to keep

effects.log: It is softer than any silk you have touched. A soldier turns his head as you go. You do not look back.

events.text: Night falls with you still on the road, and the battle begins all around you. Arrows hiss through the dark and vanish an arm's length from your face. Horses gallop through you and leave a chill in your bones. You crouch in a ditch until the drums go quiet near dawn, and count the hours by them.

choices.text: Use the noise to practise breathing under fear

effects.log: By dawn your heart keeps its own time, whatever the drums do.

choices.text: Watch how the ghost spearmen hold the line

effects.log: There is a turn of the wrist the front rank uses again and again. You will remember it.

choices.text: Sleep, if you can

effects.log: You can, a little. The dead are loud but not unkind.

events.text: The safe road follows the old supply track. At a crossroads a ghost quartermaster stands behind a cart, handing out rations to soldiers who are not there. When you pass, he holds out a cake of hard bread without looking up.

choices.text: Take the bread and thank him

effects.log: It tastes of nothing and fills you anyway. The quartermaster crosses something off a list that is nine hundred years long.

choices.text: Ask him how long he has been here

effects.log: "Since the second day," he says. "The general said keep the carts moving. So I keep them moving." He gives you two cakes.

choices.text: Refuse politely and walk on

effects.log: He lowers the bread. Somewhere behind you, another soldier who is not there takes it.

events.text: The safe road is safe from the dead, not the living. At the old bridge a party from a rival sect has stretched a rope across the way. "Toll," says their leader, a broad young man with a polished glaive. "Your find, or an hour of your blood."

choices.text: Refuse, and walk through the rope

ok.log: The rope parts against your chest. Nobody quite wants to be first. You walk on, and they let you.

fail.log: They want to be first after all. You get across, but it costs you.

choices.text: Pay them in silver instead

effects.log: The glaive-bearer weighs the purse and steps aside. A cheap bridge, as these things go.

choices.text: Go back and find another crossing

effects.log: It costs you half a day in the mud. You arrive filthy and unhurt.

events.text: The beast road runs through the crow marsh. The crows here are the size of dogs, with beaks of old iron, and they have spent nine centuries picking at armour. They have not forgotten that armour once had soldiers inside it.

choices.text: Fight your way through the flock

ok.log: You break wings and beaks and come out the other side with feathers in your hair and a crow's iron beak as a keepsake.

fail.log: They come in waves. You get through, bleeding from a dozen small cuts.

choices.text: Throw them your rations and run

effects.log: They fight over the bread instead of you. Hungry, but whole.

choices.text: Move only when the flock is eating

effects.log: It takes all afternoon, a step at a time. Patience is a martial art too.

events.text: In a fold of the plain a herd of war horses grazes on nothing. They are mist inside their ribs and iron at their hooves, and one of them, a tall grey with a broken bridle, walks up to you and lowers its head, as if waiting for a rider it lost a long time ago.

choices.text: Mount it

ok.log: It carries you across half the beast road in an hour, so smooth you barely feel the ground, and then dissolves under you like breath on a mirror.

fail.log: It bucks once, hard, and you land in the mud. It looks at you, disappointed, and walks away.

choices.text: Take off its broken bridle

effects.log: It shakes its head, free, and gallops toward the ford with the others. You keep the bridle.

choices.text: Leave the dead their horses

effects.log: The grey watches you go for a long time.

events.text: The hidden road is a trench nobody else can see, dug into the side of the hill, and you know it because you dug it. Not in this life. But your hands remember the shape of the spade, and halfway along it you find a shield with a mark cut into its rim: a mark you still make, without thinking, on things you mean to come back for.

choices.text: Take the shield

effects.log: It fits your arm as if it had been waiting. You carry it to the end of the trench and leave it there for the next time.

choices.text: Cut your mark again, fresh, beside the old one

effects.log: Two marks, two lives. The trench will keep them both.

choices.text: Walk fast and do not think about it

effects.log: Some memories are a road, not a home. You arrive early and alone.

events.text: The hidden road runs past the place where a past life of yours died. You know it the way you know a scar. There are no bones; the realm keeps nothing of the living. But a sword lies rusting in the grass, and the grass around it grows in a ring, as if something under it were still breathing.

choices.text: Pick up the sword and say the old name

effects.log: You do not know the name until you say it. The rust flakes away a little at the hilt.

choices.text: Leave a coin on the place

effects.log: You never know what the dead want. A coin is a fair guess.

choices.text: Kneel there until the shaking stops

effects.log: It takes longer than you would like. When you stand, you are steadier than you have been in years.

events.text: Ghost cavalry comes across the plain in a line a mile long, and you are too weak to fight it and too slow to run. You throw yourself into a shell crater full of rainwater and lie there while the hooves pass over, one rank after another, close enough to feel the cold.

choices.text: Hold your breath and count the ranks

effects.log: Forty ranks. You will tell this story for the rest of your life, and nobody will believe the number.

choices.text: Open your eyes and watch them pass

effects.log: You see the riders' faces: young, tired, far from home. Something in you grows up a little.

choices.text: Pray to whatever listens on a battlefield

effects.log: Something does. Or the cavalry simply passes. Either way, you live.

events.text: At the dry ford you meet your rival coming the other way, mud to the knees, spear in hand. For a moment the two of you stand on the old riverbed, and the ghosts of nine hundred years ago charge past on either side as if you were two stones in the stream.

choices.text: Nod, and step aside to let your rival pass

effects.log: A nod comes back. Not friendship. Respect, which is rarer.

choices.text: Cross spears, here and now

ok.log: Three exchanges, and your rival steps back first. Neither of you says anything. Both of you will remember.

fail.log: Three exchanges, and you are the one who steps back. It burns all the way to the guardian.

choices.text: Say the guardian is the real enemy

effects.log: Your rival laughs. "For now." But the spear comes down.

events.arc: The Boy with the Ninth Banner
events.text: Ok-bin walks beside you with the Ninth Banner held high, and the dead step aside for it: cavalry wheels away, archers lower their bows. On the long road he reads you his letter, over and over, in a voice that cracks. It says he is well, that he has new boots, that she must get on the boat. It says nothing about the ninth night.

choices.text: Ask him to read it once more

effects.log: He reads it again, slower, and this time you learn it by heart.

choices.text: Tell him his mother would be proud

effects.log: "She would be cross," he says. "I lied about the boots." He laughs, and the banner flaps.

choices.text: Ask him to show you the way the banner goes

effects.log: He takes you along the line the Ninth Banner held. Every step of it is a lesson in holding ground.

events.arc: The Boy with the Ninth Banner
events.text: Ok-bin walks beside you with the banner, quiet now. The dead step out of its way. After a long time he asks what the world is like, nine hundred years on. Do people still eat rice cakes at the new year? Is there still a river at Dallae? Do they sing about the ford?

choices.text: Tell him they still eat rice cakes

effects.log: He smiles for the first time. "Good. Good. That is enough, then."

choices.text: Tell him honestly that nobody remembers the ford

effects.log: He nods. "Then you remember it," he says. "That will do." The banner seems lighter in his hands.

choices.text: Promise to make them sing about it

effects.log: He laughs. "You cannot sing." But he holds the banner higher all the way to the general.

events.text: Ghost cavalry comes out of the evening mist, and Hyeon Mu-gyeol's lance is at your back before you call for it. Back to back you hold a hollow for an hour while the riders break against you like surf. Afterward, breathing hard, he admits it: the Red Lance Hall will expel him if he comes home without the art.

choices.text: Promise to let him study the art if you win it

effects.log: He stares at you. Then he bows, low, the first time you have seen him bow to anyone.

choices.text: Tell him a hall that expels its best is not worth going home to

effects.log: He is silent for a long time. "Maybe," he says. Something between you shifts.

choices.text: Say nothing; the truce ends at the guardian

effects.log: He nods. He knew. You walk the rest of the road a few paces apart.

events.text: You find Hyeon Mu-gyeol pinned under a fallen chariot in a gully, one leg trapped, his lance out of reach. Ghost horses are coming down the slope; you can hear them. He sees you and says nothing. He will not ask. The race, it seems, is yours to win, if you want to win it this way.

choices.text: Lift the chariot off him

effects.log: It takes everything you have. He rolls free just as the horses arrive, and the two of you hold the gully together till dawn.

choices.text: Throw him his lance and keep going

effects.log: He catches it. Whether he gets out is his own business now. You hear the fight behind you for a long time.

choices.text: Leave him

effects.log: You climb out of the gully and do not look back. The horses are loud, then quiet.

events.text: Gu Bok-rye walks with you, slow but sure, a walking stick made from a spear shaft. She knows every hollow. "The cavalry goes around that hill at moonrise. The archers never shoot east, nobody knows why. And the general," she says, "the general stands at the ford every night and asks the same question, and nobody ever answers him."

choices.text: Ask what the question is

effects.log: "Whether the city got out," she says. "I never told him. I was afraid of his face." She looks at you sidelong. "Maybe you will."

choices.text: Ask her what sixty years alone was like

effects.log: "Not alone," she says. "Loud." She laughs, then stops laughing. You walk on together a while without talking.

choices.text: Carry her pack for her

effects.log: She protests, then lets you. Her pack holds a pot, a blanket, and sixty years of letters she never sent.

events.text: Whatever happened at the ford, you will remember the general's eyes. Under the iron mask they are a man's eyes, tired past all telling, looking at something behind you: the far bank, where a city once stood. For nine hundred years he has held this ground. He did not choose to hold it so long.

choices.text: Bow to him before you go

effects.log: He does not see it. You do it anyway, for yourself.

choices.text: Remember the way he stood

effects.log: Feet wide, weight low, the spear never further than a breath from guard. You will stand like that for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Look at the far bank too

effects.log: Nothing there but grass. For a moment, though, you think you see boats.

events.text: When it is over the drums under the earth stop, all at once, for the first time since you came in. In the silence you can hear the grass, and your own breathing, and far off, the ghost of a river that has been dry for centuries. Then, slowly, the drums begin again.

choices.text: Listen to the silence while it lasts

effects.log: Three breaths of quiet in nine hundred years. You were here for them.

choices.text: Get moving before the army forms again

effects.log: Sensible. You are on the gate road before the first rank stands.

choices.text: Count the beats when they start again

effects.log: Nine beats, then a pause, then nine more. Nine days, nine nights. Even the drum remembers.

events.text: The ghost general goes down on one knee in the dry ford, his spear across his thighs, and the army behind him lowers its weapons rank by rank. He lifts his masked face to you. "Tell me," he says, in a voice like a door that has not opened in an age. "Did the city get out?"

choices.text: Tell him yes: every boat, nine hundred years ago

effects.log: He bows his head. The mask cracks down the middle. "Then we held." Behind him, a whole army sighs like wind in grass.

choices.text: Tell him you do not know

effects.log: He nods slowly, as if that were the answer he expected. He holds the spear art out to you anyway. "Find out for me."

choices.text: Tell him the city fell

effects.log: You will never know why you said it. He gets up. The battle goes on. You have the art, and a cold place in your chest.

events.text: The general falls, and the army does not. Ten thousand ghosts stand in their ranks, looking at you, waiting for an order. You realise, slowly, what they are waiting for. You beat their general. On this field, that makes you the one who gives the orders now.

choices.text: Order them to stand down

effects.log: Rank by rank they ground their spears and sit in the grass, and for one night the battle does not begin.

choices.text: Order them to march for Dallae

effects.log: They turn as one and march east, toward a city that is not there. You watch them go until they are mist.

choices.text: Say nothing and take the art

effects.log: They wait all night. In the morning they are fighting again, as if you had never come.

events.text: He beats you into the mud of the ford in four strokes, and does not bother with a fifth. Lying there, blood in your mouth, you hear him say, almost kindly: "You are not the army I am waiting for. Go home." The ghost soldiers step around you as they march.

choices.text: Get up and ask what army he waits for

effects.log: "The one that comes over the ford," he says. "It has not come yet." He does not hit you again. That is its own lesson.

choices.text: Crawl away and live

effects.log: There is no shame in living. You will tell yourself that for weeks.

choices.text: Swear you will come back stronger

effects.log: He has heard that oath before, from better than you. He does not laugh. That is worse.

events.text: You knew before you raised your weapon that he was far beyond you. You raised it anyway. The general broke your guard, your stance and very nearly your nerve, and then stopped, his spear point a finger from your throat, and looked at you for a long moment before he turned away.

choices.text: Thank him for the lesson

effects.log: Nobody has ever thanked him. His step falters, just once.

choices.text: Remember exactly how he broke your guard

effects.log: Three movements. You will practise against them for years, and never be broken that way again.

choices.text: Lie still until the army passes

effects.log: It passes. You are alive. That was more than you had any right to.

events.text: You do the only thing that can work: you fall in among the dead. Head down, steps matched to theirs, you march with the Ninth Banner through the general's own ranks, so close you could touch his stirrup. He never turns his head. On the far side of the ford you step out of the line, and nobody stops you.

choices.text: Look back once at the general

effects.log: He is looking at the far bank, as always. You were never the thing he was watching for.

choices.text: Keep marching a little longer, for the soldiers

effects.log: Ten more steps, in time with them. A soldier beside you nods. You do not know why that matters, but it does.

choices.text: Run for the gate road

effects.log: You do not stop running till the drums are faint.

events.text: A ghost sentry sees you creeping along the riverbank and calls the alarm, and the whole army turns its head at once. You run. Arrows that are not quite there tear through your sleeves and leave cold welts on your skin. You get out of the ford with the general's eyes on your back the whole way.

choices.text: Hide in the reeds until dark

effects.log: They forget you by moonrise. The dead have short memories for the living.

choices.text: Remember where the sentries stand, for next time

effects.log: Every opening, every life, the same posts. Now you know them.

choices.text: Call your name back at the general as you run

effects.log: Foolish. Somewhere in that iron mask, he hears it.

events.text: The general raises his spear, then stops. He is looking at your stance: the way your back foot turns, the way your hands sit. "I know that guard," he says. "I taught it to a soldier, once. Or the soldier taught it to me." Some life of yours fought beside him, or against him. He cannot remember which, and neither can you.

choices.text: Ask him to fight you the old way, to remember

effects.log: You trade blows like two old friends sparring. When it ends, you both know a little more than before.

choices.text: Tell him you were his soldier

effects.log: You do not know if it is true. He lowers his head, and you think it might be.

choices.text: Change your guard, so he cannot know you

effects.log: It is a cold thing to do to a ghost. It works.

events.text: This is the ford where you died. The general killed you here, in a life you only half remember: a thrust under the arm, the cold water, the drum. Now you stand on the same stones, and this time it has gone differently. The general does not know you. You know him very well.

choices.text: Let the old fear go

effects.log: It does not go easily, but it goes. Something that has followed your soul for lifetimes stays behind in the ford.

choices.text: Say aloud: "Not this time"

effects.log: The ghosts nearest you turn their heads. The words carry over the water.

choices.text: Touch the stone where you fell

effects.log: It is cold. Only cold. You are alive.

events.text: Your rival reached the ford first and is already fighting the general when you arrive, giving ground step by step. For one bad moment you could simply wait, and let the general do your work for you.

choices.text: Throw yourself into the fight beside your rival

effects.log: Two against one, and the general still nearly wins. Afterward neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Wait, and let your rival tire the general out

effects.log: It works. Your rival sees you do it, and will not forget.

choices.text: Shout a warning about the general's left side

effects.log: Your rival hears, and lives. A debt, now, whether either of you likes it.

events.arc: The Boy with the Ninth Banner
events.text: At the end of it Ok-bin walks past you into the ford, plants the Ninth Banner in the dry riverbed, and salutes his general. "Sir," he says, his voice cracking. "The boats are away. The city got out. We can stop." The ghost general looks at the boy for a long time. Then he takes off his iron mask, and he is only an old soldier, crying.

choices.text: Stand to attention beside the boy

effects.log: You stand with them while the sun comes up. For the first time in nine hundred years, the drums do not begin.

choices.text: Look away, and give them this

effects.log: Some things are not for the living to watch. You hear the general laugh, once, like a man.

choices.text: Ask the general for the art in the boy's name

effects.log: "Take it," he says, not looking at you. "Take it all." He only has eyes for the boy.

events.arc: The Boy with the Ninth Banner
events.text: It goes wrong at the ford, and when the general's spear comes for you it is Ok-bin who stands in the way, the Ninth Banner held up between you and the spear. "Sir," he says, shaking. "Not this one. This one is carrying my letter." The general stops. For a long time nobody on the whole battlefield moves. Then the spear goes up, and the army moves on without you.

choices.text: Get up and thank the boy

effects.log: "Soldiers do not thank each other," he says. "They just remember." He grins at you, grey and young.

choices.text: Ask him to come with you to the gate

effects.log: He looks at the general's back. "After," he says. "I have to tell him first." He follows the army toward the ford.

choices.text: Lie in the grass and breathe

effects.log: You are alive because a boy who died nine hundred years ago was braver than you. You will think about that for a long time.

events.text: When the general falls, Hyeon Mu-gyeol is at your shoulder, breathing hard, his crimson sleeve torn. He looks at the spear art lying on the dry stones of the ford, then at you. "You won it," he says, and the words cost him. "Show me one form. Just one. Then I will know what I lost to."

choices.text: Show him the first form, slowly

effects.log: He watches with his whole body. When you finish, he bows, and his eyes are wet. "Thank you."

choices.text: Show him all of it

effects.log: It takes until dusk. By the end, you understand the art better for having taught it.

choices.text: Tell him it is not yours to show yet

effects.log: He nods, stiff, and steps back. The truce, it seems, is over.

events.text: It goes wrong, and Hyeon Mu-gyeol drags you out of the ford by your collar while the army marches over the place you were lying. He props you against a broken chariot. "We are even," he says, though you are not sure you were ever owed. "Next opening, I will beat him. You can watch."

choices.text: Tell him you will be there

effects.log: "Good," he says. "Bring better footwork." It is the closest he comes to friendship.

choices.text: Ask him to teach you the Red Lance forms

effects.log: He laughs, then sees you mean it. He shows you three, in the chariot's shadow.

choices.text: Say nothing, too tired to speak

effects.log: He sits down beside you, and the two of you watch the ghosts fight till dawn.

events.text: Hyeon Mu-gyeol is waiting at the ford, not to fight the general but to watch you do it, and when it is over he comes down from the ridge with his lance at the ready and nothing in his face at all. "The race," he says, "was always to the gate. Not to the guardian." He bows, too politely, and leaves.

choices.text: Call after him that you will be ready

effects.log: He raises one hand without turning. You believe him.

choices.text: Let him go, and rest

effects.log: Whatever waits at the gate can wait. You sleep in the shadow of a chariot.

choices.text: Follow him to see where he goes

effects.log: He goes to a hollow near the gate road and sits down to wait. Now you know where.

events.text: Gu Bok-rye watched it all from the ridge, leaning on her spear-shaft stick. When it is over she comes down into the ford, slowly, and stands where the general stood. "Sixty years," she says, "and I never came this close." She touches the dry stones with her stick, as if to make sure they are real. "Did he ask you? About the city?"

choices.text: Tell her he asked, and what you answered

effects.log: She listens with her eyes closed. "Good," she says. "Somebody finally told him something." She seems lighter.

choices.text: Tell her she should have come down years ago

effects.log: "I know," she says. "Fear keeps you alive. It also keeps you on a hill for sixty years." She laughs, and it is a young laugh.

choices.text: Give her a piece of what you found

effects.log: She turns it over in her old hands for a long time. "I came in for this," she says. "I was nineteen." She gives it back.

events.text: It goes badly at the ford, and it is Gu Bok-rye who drags you into her trench as the army marches past, an old woman with the grip of a blacksmith. She binds your hurts with strips of a robe sixty years out of fashion and feeds you grass soup. "Everyone loses to him," she says. "I lost to him at nineteen. That is how I missed the gate."

choices.text: Ask her to wake you in time for the gate

effects.log: "I will not make that mistake twice," she says, and sits up all night with her stick across her knees.

choices.text: Ask how she lost to him

effects.log: She shows you, with the stick, slowly. It is the same mistake you made. You will not make it again.

choices.text: Sleep

effects.log: You sleep in a trench on a battlefield, guarded by a stranger who has had sixty years to grow kind. It is the best sleep of the realm.

events.text: The gate opens at the edge of the plain like a tear in the sky, and every party still alive walks toward it. Behind you, as the barrier begins to seal, the drums start again, slow and patient, as if nobody had ever come. You do not turn around. Nobody does.

choices.text: Turn around anyway, at the last moment

effects.log: You see the whole plain once, rust-red under a red sky, every banner raised. Then the gate closes on it.

choices.text: Help a stranger through who is limping

effects.log: A junior from some small sect, terrified. Your shoulder gets the child out. You never learn the name.

choices.text: Walk through with your eyes shut

effects.log: The cold of the barrier, then sudden warmth, birdsong, and the smell of ordinary rain.

events.text: On the far side of the barrier it is raining: ordinary rain on ordinary fields, with birds in the hedges and a farmer cursing a stuck cart. After the battlefield it is almost too much. People who went in proud come out quiet. Some of them kneel in the mud and laugh.

choices.text: Kneel in the mud and laugh too

effects.log: It feels foolish and wonderful. The farmer stares at all of you as if you were mad.

choices.text: Help the farmer with the cart

effects.log: He thanks you and asks where you have been. You find you cannot explain it.

choices.text: Count who came out, and who did not

effects.log: Fewer than went in. You remember the faces, for whatever good it does.

events.text: At the gate you hand the dead general's spear art to the senior of {sr_sect}'s party, and watch it vanish into a lacquered box with three locks. It is the safe thing. There are a lot of masked faces near the gate who saw what you carried, and none of them comes near a sect's banner.

choices.text: Ask to be the first to study it at home

effects.log: The senior writes your name on the box, first of three. It is a promise in front of witnesses.

choices.text: Say nothing; the art was never yours

effects.log: The general gave it to whoever beat him. You beat him for them. That is a kind of loyalty, too.

choices.text: Watch the masked faces as they turn away

effects.log: You will know some of them again, in some other place, by the way they walk.

events.text: You walk out under {sr_sect}'s banner with nothing to show for it but the battlefield in your eyes. Others in the party carry finds; you carry a memory of ten thousand dead men marching. The senior grips your shoulder at the gate. "You came out," the senior says. "Half the realm did not."

choices.text: Ask the senior what the realm left them

effects.log: A long silence. "My first opening, I lost a friend at the ford." It is the most the senior has ever told anyone.

choices.text: Promise yourself the next realm will be different

effects.log: Promises made at a closing gate have a way of being kept.

choices.text: Be glad to be alive, and say so

effects.log: Several of the party laugh, and then agree. It is a good walk home.

events.text: The spear art is in your robe, against your skin: a roll of hide covered in the general's own cramped hand, nine forms for nine days. You keep your face still at the gate. You are not the only one who knows what came out of the ford, and some of the eyes on you are not friendly.

choices.text: Walk out with the parties, in plain sight

effects.log: Safety in a crowd. Nobody makes a move with a hundred witnesses watching.

choices.text: Read the first form before you leave the realm

effects.log: You read it by the light of the closing gate. The first form is simple, and endless.

choices.text: Wrap it in the silk of a fallen banner

effects.log: It seems right. The general's art should leave the field in the colours of his army.

events.text: They were waiting just inside the gate, masked, five of them, and they wanted the spear art. They did not get it. You come out of the realm into the rain with your robe slashed, your breath ragged, and the roll of hide still against your skin. Behind you the barrier closes over whatever they were.

choices.text: Hunt one of them down and unmask him

effects.log: A fighter from a sect that smiled at you at the gate. You let him go, and remember the smile.

choices.text: Keep walking and do not look back

effects.log: Wise. The rest of them are still somewhere in the crowd.

choices.text: Tell everyone at the gate what happened

effects.log: By nightfall the whole murim knows somebody tried and failed. Your name rises with the story.

events.text: Masked fighters were waiting at the gate, and whatever they came for, you have nothing of it now. You stand in the rain outside the barrier, bruised, empty-handed, alive. The realm is closing behind you. Sixty years until it opens again, and nothing in your hands to show for this one.

choices.text: Laugh, because you are alive

effects.log: It hurts to laugh. You do it anyway, and feel better.

choices.text: Memorise every voice you heard behind the masks

effects.log: Three voices. You will hear them again some day, in a teahouse or a hall, and you will know.

choices.text: Swear the next realm will not take from you

effects.log: A hard oath, sworn in the mud. It sits in your spine like iron.

events.text: You do not take the gate. While the parties crowd toward it, you find a crack low in the barrier near the dry river, the same kind you might have come in by, and you go out on your belly through cold mud. Nobody sees you leave. Nobody will know what you took out of the realm, or what you did not.

choices.text: Wait at a distance and watch the gate

effects.log: You see who waited with masks, and who walked out shaking. Knowledge is a find too.

choices.text: Go straight home

effects.log: Quiet is its own reward. You are three valleys away by dawn.

choices.text: Leave a mark by the crack for the next opening

effects.log: A scratch on a stone. Whoever comes in sixty years may thank you.

events.text: You have walked out of this gate before. Not in this life, but your body knows the cold of the barrier and the first breath of the outside, and does not flinch. Somewhere in the soul, something marks it down: twice now. The ford will still be there when the realm opens again.

choices.text: Promise the next life you will come back

effects.log: A promise to someone who is you, and is not. It feels like the right thing.

choices.text: Promise the next life you will not

effects.log: Some places should only be walked through once or twice. The soul accepts this.

choices.text: Remember everything you can, as hard as you can

effects.log: A soul keeps what it holds tightest. You hold the ford.

events.text: A life of yours went into this realm and never walked out of it. This one does. You stop just outside the barrier and breathe, and the ordinary air goes all the way down, and something that was waiting for a very long time lets go.

choices.text: Say goodbye to that other life

effects.log: You do not know its name. You say goodbye anyway. The rain carries it off.

choices.text: Thank it for the warning it left in your bones

effects.log: Every step on that field, your body knew where the danger was. That other life paid for it.

choices.text: Walk on without a word

effects.log: There is nothing to say to the dead except that you lived. You have said it.

events.text: Word of it reaches the gate before you do: somebody beat the ghost general. The young elites of a dozen sects stand aside to let you through, and an old swordsman from some far province spits on his palm and holds it up to you, the old soldier's salute. The ford will have a new story now, and your name is in it.

choices.text: Return the old soldier's salute

effects.log: He grins with three teeth. "Nine hundred years," he says. "About time."

choices.text: Say the general let you win

effects.log: Nobody believes it. The modesty spreads faster than the boast would have.

choices.text: Leave quickly before it goes to your head

effects.log: Too late, a little. But you are on the road before anyone can buy you a cup of tea.

events.arc: The Boy with the Ninth Banner
events.text: At the gate Ok-bin stops. He cannot go further; the dead of this field never can. He looks at the letter over your heart and swallows. "There is a river at Dallae," he says. "Or there was. Give it to the river. She will get it." The barrier begins to close. He lifts the Ninth Banner in salute.

choices.text: Promise to find the river

effects.log: Months later you find it: a town now, a market on the bank. You give a folded square of nothing to the water, and feel it taken.

choices.text: Read the letter aloud to him one last time

effects.log: He mouths the words with you. At "get on the boat" he smiles. Then the gate takes him.

choices.text: Salute him back, a soldier to a soldier

effects.log: He grins, grey and fourteen and nine hundred years old. "Hold the line," he says. The gate closes.

events.arc: The Boy with the Ninth Banner
events.text: At the gate Ok-bin stops, as the dead of this field must. He tears the tassel from the Ninth Banner and holds it out to you: faded red cord, nine knots. "Somebody should remember the ford," he says. "You said nobody does. So you." Behind him the field is going dim. His outline is going with it.

choices.text: Take the tassel and tie it to your weapon

effects.log: You carry it for the rest of your life. When people ask, you tell them about the ford, and they remember.

choices.text: Ask him his mother's name

effects.log: "Ok-sun," he says. "She made the best rice cakes in Dallae." You will remember that too.

choices.text: Tell him he can stop holding the banner now

effects.log: He looks at it in his hands as if he had never thought of that. Then he lets it fall, and is gone, smiling.

events.text: Hyeon Mu-gyeol walks out of the gate beside you, his lance on his shoulder, and the Red Lance Hall's party waiting there goes quiet when they see who he is walking with. He stops. "If the hall throws me out," he says, "I will find you. You owe me a spar." It is not a threat. You are fairly sure it is not a threat.

choices.text: Tell him your door is open

effects.log: He nods once. Years later, when he knocks, you will remember this gate.

choices.text: Spar with him now, in front of his hall

effects.log: Ten exchanges in the rain. His hall sees him fight as an equal beside the one who took the art. Whatever they do to him, they will remember that.

choices.text: Tell him to go home and win his place

effects.log: He laughs. "That is the plan." He walks to his hall with his head up.

events.text: Hyeon Mu-gyeol is waiting at the gate with a dozen fighters of the Red Lance Hall, one crimson sleeve stiff with old mud. You left him under a chariot with the horses coming. He got out. He looks at you for a long moment, and the whole hall waits for him to say a word. He says, "Go." Just that.

choices.text: Go

effects.log: You go. You will never know why he let you. It sits in you like a stone for years.

choices.text: Apologise, in front of his hall

effects.log: His face does not change. "Go," he says again, but quieter. It is not forgiveness. It is the start of a road to it.

choices.text: Tell him you would do it again

effects.log: A murmur goes through the hall. He only nods, as if you had confirmed something. You have made an enemy for life.

events.text: At the gate Hyeon Mu-gyeol falls into step beside you and says nothing for a while. "You were faster," he says at last, the words dragged out of him. "This time." Then he is gone into the crowd of his hall, and you know you will see that crimson sleeve again, at some other gate, in some other year.

choices.text: Call after him: "Next time"

effects.log: His hand goes up without his turning. It is a promise, from both of you.

choices.text: Let him go without a word

effects.log: Some rivals are best left a little hungry.

choices.text: Send him a note later, with one form of the art

effects.log: Weeks later, a reply: one form of the Red Lance, exactly drawn. Neither of you mentions the gate.

events.text: Gu Bok-rye stands at the gate with her pot on her back and her stick in her hand, and does not move. Sixty years. You take her arm, as you promised, and the two of you walk through the barrier together into the rain. She stops on the other side and turns her face up, and the rain runs down it. "It is so quiet," she says.

choices.text: Take her home with you

effects.log: She lives with you a while, then finds a small house by a river. Every spring she sends grass soup. You eat it all.

choices.text: Take her to what is left of her sect's mountain

effects.log: Nothing is left but a gate post. She sits by it and talks to it for an hour, then asks to go somewhere warm.

choices.text: Give her silver for a new life

effects.log: She looks at the coins as if they were a foreign country. "I will learn," she says.

events.text: Gu Bok-rye walks you to the gate and stops a step short of it. "I thought about it all night," she says. "Out there, everyone I knew is dead. In here, at least, the dead are company." She presses her sixty years of unsent letters into your hands. "Post them. Some of the houses may still stand."

choices.text: Post every letter

effects.log: Most come back. Three do not. One day, a woman you never met writes to thank you for her grandmother's letter.

choices.text: Argue with her one more time

effects.log: She smiles and shakes her head. "Go on. You will miss the gate. I know about that."

choices.text: Promise to come back for her next opening

effects.log: Sixty years. She laughs. "I will keep the soup warm." You both know she will not see it. You promise anyway.

events.text: The way into {sr_realm} is a whirlpool in the middle of Lake Mireu, and you go down it like a leaf. The water closes over you, green and then blue and then black, and just when your lungs begin to burn you fall out of it onto dry tiles, gasping, in a bubble of air the size of a courtyard. Above you, through a ceiling of water, the sun is a coin.

choices.text: Lie still and get your breath back

effects.log: You lie on six-hundred-year-old tiles and breathe. The air tastes of lotus and cold stone.

choices.text: Look up at the sun until your eyes adjust

effects.log: Fish drift across it like slow birds. You learn the way the light bends here; it will matter.

choices.text: Get up at once and find the walls

effects.log: The bubble ends in a wall of water you can push your hand into. Beyond it, rooftops, and more rooftops.

events.text: The first hall is dry, its air trapped under a great tiled roof, and full of people. Courtiers in robes of every rank stand bowing toward a throne room far below, frozen at the deepest point of the bow, and every one of them is pearl: white, smooth, faintly shining. A minister's hat has rolled off one bowed head. Nobody has picked it up in six hundred years.

choices.text: Put the hat back on the minister's head

effects.log: It fits. The pearl face does not change, but the hall feels less sad, somehow.

choices.text: Bow as they bow, toward the throne

effects.log: You hold the bow a breath too long, and something deep below seems to notice.

choices.text: Study the faces for some clue to what happened

ok.log: Every face shows surprise, none shows fear. Whatever drowned them came gently, in their sleep. You will remember that at the dragon.

fail.log: They are only faces. You stare until your eyes ache and learn nothing but how lonely the place is.

events.text: The party from {sr_sect} ropes itself together at the edge of the whirlpool, one cord around every waist, the way the sect records say the last expedition did. The senior in charge checks every knot twice. "The lake will try to separate us," the senior says. "Do not let it. If the cord goes slack, pull."

choices.text: Tie your knot the way the senior shows you

effects.log: It holds all the way down. The senior notices, and nods.

choices.text: Volunteer to go first down the whirlpool

effects.log: You go first, and the whole party comes down your line. They will remember who led.

choices.text: Ask what happened to the last expedition

effects.log: "Four came back," the senior says. "Of eleven." Nobody talks much after that.

events.text: The crack in this barrier is an old well in a farmer's yard three miles from the lake. The farmer charges you nothing and watches you climb down with deep pity. Forty rungs, then water, then a long swim through black stone, and you come up inside the palace well, in a kitchen courtyard where pearl cooks still stir pearl pots.

choices.text: Leave a coin on the well's rim for the farmer

effects.log: When you climb out, three days later, a bowl of rice is waiting by the coin.

choices.text: Taste the water in the pots

effects.log: It is only lake water. But it is cold enough to make your teeth ache and your mind very clear.

choices.text: Keep moving before anyone sees you

effects.log: Nobody does. The cooks have their backs to you, as they have for six centuries.

events.text: You have never been inside a great realm before, and nothing could have prepared you for fish swimming through a window into a king's palace. They are as long as your arm and as gold as old coins, and they circle you with the bored curiosity of guards who have seen a great many visitors, and outlasted all of them.

choices.text: Hold out your hand to the nearest one

effects.log: It noses your palm, decides you are not food, and swims away. It feels like a judgement.

choices.text: Follow them; fish know the way through water

effects.log: They lead you to an open gate you would have missed. Good guards, after all.

choices.text: Write the first thing you saw on your sleeve, to remember

effects.log: "Fish in the windows." You will laugh at it later, when you are old.

events.text: The tiles of the entry court are laid in a pattern of waves and cranes, and your feet know it. In some other life you walked these halls; maybe you drowned in them, maybe you only got lost. Your body turns left at the second crane without asking you, toward a door you have never seen, which is exactly where you remember it.

choices.text: Trust your feet and follow them

effects.log: They take you through three halls by the shortest way, past a niche where a lamp still burns that you think you lit.

choices.text: Stop and try to remember the life

effects.log: Pieces: a rope going slack, a voice calling your name, a kind of peace. Not enough for a story. Enough to be careful.

choices.text: Turn right on purpose, to be someone new

effects.log: The right-hand way is slower and stranger. It is also yours alone.

events.text: Your lungs remember this place before you do. The moment the water closes over you they seize, the old animal panic of drowning, and you know with total certainty that some life of yours ended in this lake. You claw your way into the air of the first hall and kneel on the tiles, shaking.

choices.text: Breathe slowly until the old fear passes

effects.log: It passes. This lungful is yours, not that other life's. You stand.

choices.text: Tell the fear: not this time

effects.log: Out loud, to an empty hall. The pearl courtiers do not answer, but the shaking stops.

choices.text: Go back up and come down again, on purpose

effects.log: Twice through the whirlpool, by choice. The second time your lungs know who is in charge.

events.text: You have been through enough realms to know that each one has a pulse. This one has the slowest of any: a great breath in, a great breath out, once in an hour, that moves the currents through every hall. The dragon is breathing. Every route through the palace is easier going with the breath than against it.

choices.text: Teach the juniors to swim with the breath

effects.log: Most of them do not understand. Two do, and come through the halls with you like fish.

choices.text: Time your own moves by it, alone

effects.log: You go through the halls with the current at your back and arrive before anyone.

choices.text: Sit and listen to the dragon breathe

effects.log: An hour passes. Then another. Something in your own breath slows to match it.

events.text: The cold of the lake gets into old bones in a way the young ones do not feel. They are laughing on the tiles of the first hall, wringing out their sleeves. You are working out how long your joints will let you swim before they lock. Not as long as theirs. Long enough, if you are clever.

choices.text: Swim less and think more

effects.log: You find the dry ways through the roofs while the young ones swim the corridors. You arrive drier and sooner.

choices.text: Rub warmth into your hands with your qi

effects.log: Old tricks are old because they work. The cold backs off.

choices.text: Let a young one help you over the wall

effects.log: The child is delighted to be useful. You learn the name and remember it.

events.text: The deeper you go, the heavier the water, and the heavier the realm. The guardian here is so far above you that its presence alone presses on your chest like a hand, even through all this lake. The others go down the stair ahead of you. You stop to breathe twice on every landing.

choices.text: Go slowly; the dragon is asleep

effects.log: It is. You remind yourself of that on every step, and it is enough.

choices.text: Turn the pressure into training, one landing at a time

effects.log: By the bottom of the stair your channels ache and are wider than they were.

choices.text: Stay close to the strongest party

effects.log: Nobody notices you. The water in their wake is a little lighter.

events.text: A bubble rises past you in the first flooded corridor, and inside it, upside down, grinning, is your rival's face, gone ahead of you by some trick of the currents. Your rival waves. The bubble bursts on the ceiling. The race to the pearl, it seems, began without you.

choices.text: Swim harder

effects.log: You catch up by the third hall and pass your rival on the stair. A grin, a rude gesture, and the race is even.

choices.text: Let your rival go ahead and spring the traps

effects.log: Two halls later you pass a net of old wire, freshly cut. Thank you, rival.

choices.text: Wave back, cheerfully

effects.log: You hear a laugh echo through the water. Rivals can be good company too.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: There is music under the lake. You hear it through the water before you see anything: a zither, slow, the same few bars again and again, a lullaby. In a dry hall off the main stair a woman in court robes sits playing it, her hair afloat as if she were still under water. Two strings are left on her instrument. "Quietly," she says, without stopping. "He is asleep."

choices.text: Offer to find her new strings

effects.log: She looks up for the first time. "In the treasury," she says. "Silk from the south, in a pearl box. Please." Her name is Ga-ram.

choices.text: Ask her why she plays

effects.log: "If I stop, he wakes," she says. "If he wakes, the lake rises over the hills above. I have played for six hundred years. I am very tired."

choices.text: Back away, quietly

effects.log: She nods, grateful, and goes on playing. The lullaby follows you down the stair for a long time.

events.text: At the whirlpool's edge a young woman in the sleek blue robes of the Clear Tide Sect is holding a bead that glows like a drop of moonlight. "A breathing bead," she says. "Enough air for two, if two are careful. I am Pyo Seol-ah. I need someone who can fight, and you need someone who can breathe. Well?"

choices.text: Accept her offer

effects.log: She grins and loops the bead's cord around both your wrists. "Do not swim faster than me," she says. "Ever."

choices.text: Ask what she really wants down there

effects.log: The grin goes. "My master is dying of a cold that only a dragon pearl can draw out. I do not want the pearl. I want one touch of it."

choices.text: Tell her you breathe on your own

effects.log: She shrugs. "Then breathe." She goes down the whirlpool alone, and you think about her bead for the next three halls.

events.arc: The King Who Bound the Dragon
events.text: From somewhere far below, through the water and the stone, a voice is calling. It is old and very patient, and it says the same thing over and over: "Is anyone there? Anyone at all?" The other entrants pretend not to hear it. One of them, an old hand, says flatly: "Do not answer the king."

choices.text: Answer him

effects.log: "Yes," you call down the stair. The voice stops. Then, very quietly: "Come down. Please. It has been so long."

choices.text: Go down quietly and look first

effects.log: You follow the voice down five stairs without a word and see, through a flooded door, a throne, and a chain of gold.

choices.text: Take the old hand's advice

effects.log: You do not answer. The voice goes on calling all the time you are in the palace.

events.text: The way down leads through the great procession hall, where the whole court was walking in state the night the lake rose. Musicians, banner bearers, ministers, guards: pearl, all of them, in mid-step, with fish drifting between their sleeves. At the very end of the procession, small and alone, a pearl child is carrying the king's parasol.

choices.text: Straighten the child's parasol

effects.log: It was tilting. You set it right, and feel as if someone, somewhere, has said thank you.

choices.text: Walk the procession's route, in step

effects.log: It takes you the long way, the way of ceremony. Ceremony knew where the floors were sound.

choices.text: Swim over their heads, fast

effects.log: Faster, and colder. You come down by the throne stair shivering, and ahead.

events.text: A bubble of air rises out of a crack in the floor and bursts against your face, and for a moment you hear a voice inside it: a woman laughing, six hundred years ago, at some joke nobody remembers. More bubbles follow. The whole palace is full of trapped moments, breathing out one at a time.

choices.text: Catch the next bubble and listen

effects.log: Two people arguing about the price of fish. You laugh out loud, alone in a drowned palace.

choices.text: Follow the bubbles back to where they come from

effects.log: A cracked jar under the floor, still full of old air. You take a breath of the past. It tastes of plum blossom and old rain.

choices.text: Let them go by and keep moving

effects.log: Some laughter belongs to the dead. You leave it to them.

events.text: The safe road is the royal causeway, a dry stone walk roofed with trapped air, and every party in the realm is on it. Halfway along, a rival sect has stretched a net across the way and is checking packs. "Anyone carrying lake treasure pays a share," their leader says.

choices.text: Tell them you are carrying nothing, and stare

ok.log: They look at you, decide you are not worth it, and lift the net.

fail.log: They do not believe you, and search you. Nothing to find, but your dignity stays behind on the causeway.

choices.text: Go under the causeway instead, through the water

effects.log: Cold, black and quiet. You come up beyond the net, blue-lipped and unseen.

choices.text: Pay them a little silver to keep the peace

effects.log: Cheap at the price, in a place like this.

events.text: On the royal causeway one of the pearl ministers is not quite pearl. His eyes move. He has been standing in the same place so long that the pearl is only a crust over him, and when you pass he whispers, without moving his lips: "The tribute list. Has anyone sent the tribute list?"

choices.text: Tell him the tribute was sent

effects.log: A tiny sigh. The crust over him cracks, and something inside goes quiet and still at last.

choices.text: Ask him what he remembers of the night

effects.log: "The king said the chain would hold. Then the water was warm, and we were tired." He says nothing more.

choices.text: Walk on before he asks again

effects.log: Behind you he asks the next passer-by. And the next.

events.text: The beast road goes through the drowned water gardens, and the water gardens belong to the eels: dozens of them, thick as a young tree, the colour of jade, with teeth like a comb. They lie in the old lotus beds and watch you come with eyes that have seen a great many swimmers and remembered all of them.

choices.text: Swim straight through

ok.log: You come out of the lotus beds with a bite in your sleeve and three eels sulking behind you.

fail.log: They are faster than you in their own water. You get through, and it costs you.

choices.text: Throw them your rations and go while they fight

effects.log: Hungry the rest of the way, but whole.

choices.text: Wait for the dragon's breath to carry you past

effects.log: The current comes once an hour. When it does, it takes you over the gardens like a leaf.

events.text: The palace kitchens are flooded, and the crabs that live there now are the size of cartwheels, their shells grown over with old pots and ladles. They have no interest in you until you come near the great stove, where something glints in the ash: a cook's jade ring, and two spirit stones.

choices.text: Go for the stove anyway

ok.log: You snatch it all and are out of the kitchen before the crabs have finished turning round.

fail.log: A claw catches your leg. You get away, without the ring and with a limp.

choices.text: Leave the crabs their kitchen

effects.log: Some treasure is guarded for good reasons.

choices.text: Lure them away with a dropped ladle

effects.log: An old ladle, clanging down the corridor. They go after it like children. You take a ring nobody will miss.

events.text: The hidden road is the servants' stair, behind a panel in the procession hall that you open before you know why. It is dry, narrow, and steep, and halfway down, tucked into a gap in the stone, is a bundle wrapped in oiled cloth: a lamp, flint, and a note in a hand you somehow know. It says only: "Left at the bottom. Not right."

choices.text: Go left at the bottom

effects.log: Right would have been a flooded shaft. Your past self knew.

choices.text: Add a note of your own to the bundle

effects.log: "Still left. Still not right." For whoever you are next.

choices.text: Light the lamp and keep it

effects.log: It burns with a small green flame that never seems to use up the oil.

events.text: The servants' stair passes a small room you have seen before: the room where some life of yours drowned. A rope still lies coiled on the floor, its end frayed. The air here is thin and old. You understand, standing in the doorway, that you were alone, and that you were not afraid at the end.

choices.text: Coil the rope neatly and leave it

effects.log: A small tidiness for a life that ended here. The room feels finished.

choices.text: Take the frayed end with you

effects.log: A short length of old rope, tied to your belt. Some memories are worth carrying.

choices.text: Say the name you think you had

effects.log: You are not sure of it. You say it anyway, and the bubbles in the corner rise a little faster.

events.text: The dragon breathes, and the current that comes with it is too strong for you. It takes you off your feet and drags you through three flooded halls like driftwood. The stronger entrants hold onto pillars. You hold onto nothing, and come to rest, bruised and alive, in a hall nobody else has found.

choices.text: Search the hall while you are here

effects.log: A pearl courtier's purse of old coins, and a hairpin of good jade.

choices.text: Rest until your arms stop shaking

effects.log: It takes a while. When you get up, you know the current's rhythm in your bones.

choices.text: Mark the way back for others who get swept here

effects.log: Scratches on three pillars. Somebody weaker than you will find them.

events.text: You and your rival reach the last pocket of air before the throne stair at the same moment, and it is small: enough for one to rest in properly, not two. Your rival looks at you. You look back. Water drips from both your faces.

choices.text: Share it, shoulder to shoulder

effects.log: Cramped, uncomfortable, and oddly peaceful. Neither of you says a word, and neither will forget.

choices.text: Push your rival out of it

ok.log: You win the shove. Your rival goes back into the water with a look you will see again.

fail.log: You lose the shove, and find your own pocket somewhere colder.

choices.text: Leave it to your rival and swim on

effects.log: A strange courtesy. Your rival stares after you, confused.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: The treasury is a flooded vault of drowned gold, and in the middle of it, exactly where Ga-ram said, is a box of pearl with a coil of southern silk inside, still dry. On the way back you hear her lullaby falter: one more string has gone. She is playing the whole song on one string now, and it is thinner.

choices.text: Swim back as fast as you can

effects.log: You make it. She restrings the zither with shaking hands, and the lullaby swells, full and slow, for the first time in a hundred years.

choices.text: Take a few coins of drowned gold too, on the way

effects.log: You make it back, just. The strings and the gold both. She does not ask about the gold.

choices.text: Keep the pearl box and give her only the silk

effects.log: A box of pearl is worth a fortune up above. She does not notice; she has eyes only for the silk.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: You go back to Ga-ram's hall instead of on, and sit by her while she plays. After a while, without stopping, she begins to teach you the lullaby: a hand position, a breath, a turn of the wrist. "If I stop one day," she says, "someone must know it. I would rather it were someone who came back."

choices.text: Learn it properly

effects.log: It takes hours. When you play the first bars, she closes her eyes, and the whole palace seems to settle.

choices.text: Ask her what she would do if she could stop

effects.log: "Sleep," she says. "And then go up, and see the sun." She smiles. "It is a small wish."

choices.text: Thank her and go on

effects.log: The lullaby follows you down the stair. You find you are humming it.

events.text: The bead dims in the deepest corridor, where no air pocket has survived. There is breath left in it for one, not two, and the next air is three halls away. Pyo Seol-ah looks at the bead, then at you. "I can make three halls," she says, which is not true, and you both know it.

choices.text: Give her the bead and swim

effects.log: You make three halls on your own lungs and come up on the far tiles purple and choking. She is there to pull you out.

choices.text: Take the bead and pull her behind you

effects.log: You breathe for both, a mouthful each in turn, and come up together. It is closer than either of you will admit.

choices.text: Take the bead and go

effects.log: You make the far hall. She makes it a long while after you, alone. She does not say anything. She does not need to.

events.arc: The King Who Bound the Dragon
events.text: The throne hall is the only dry room at the bottom of the palace, and King Ui-ryang sits in it, overgrown with white coral to the chest. A golden chain runs from his wrist out through the doors, into the dark, toward the dragon. "I bound it," he says. "And the bond bound me. While the chain holds, I cannot die. If someone cut it, the dragon would wake, and I would rest."

choices.text: Promise to cut the chain

effects.log: He closes his eyes. "Thank you. Be quick. When it wakes, it will be very angry, or very glad. I never knew which."

choices.text: Refuse: the dragon is safer chained

effects.log: "Yes," he says. "That is what I told myself, too, for six hundred years." He does not ask again.

choices.text: Ask him why he bound it

effects.log: "Drought," he says. "Three years of it. My people were dying." He looks at the coral on his hands. "They died anyway. Only wetter."

events.text: Whatever else you remember of the dragon, you will remember the eye: as big as a door, the colour of deep water, opening once and looking at you. There is no anger in it, and no welcome. Only a great slow interest, as if you were a new kind of fish. Then it closes again.

choices.text: Meet the eye and do not look away

effects.log: You hold it as long as it is open. Afterwards your hands shake, and your spirit is steadier than it has ever been.

choices.text: Bow to it

effects.log: A small creature bowing to a large one. It may not have noticed. The palace did.

choices.text: Remember the colour, exactly

effects.log: You will try to describe it for the rest of your life. You will never get it right.

events.text: When it is over a single scale drifts down through the water of the throne court, turning slowly, big as a shield and blue as evening. The dragon has shed it in its sleep, or in its waking. It settles at your feet on the old tiles with the softest sound.

choices.text: Take it

effects.log: It is lighter than it looks, and cold, and it hums faintly when water moves over it. A fine thing to carry out.

choices.text: Leave it where it fell

effects.log: It belongs to the palace. You feel better, somehow, for leaving it.

choices.text: Rub a little of its shine onto your hands

effects.log: A silly, old belief: dragon shine on the palms brings luck. It cannot hurt.

events.text: The dragon wakes for the fight, and fights the way rivers flood: all at once, from everywhere. You do not beat it so much as survive it long enough that it grows bored, and curls back into its coils around the tower, and lets the pearl roll from under its chin to the tiles. Whether it was defeated or only done, you will never be sure.

choices.text: Thank it before you take the pearl

effects.log: An eye opens a crack, and closes. Something passes between you.

choices.text: Take the pearl at once and go

effects.log: It is warm in your hands, and it pulses slowly, like a heart.

choices.text: Tell everyone you beat a dragon

effects.log: You will. Every one of them, for years. For now, you tell the dragon.

events.text: The dragon does not even wake up properly. Its tail moves once in its sleep, the way a cat's tail flicks at a fly, and you are thrown the length of the throne court into a pillar. You lie there in the water, unable to breathe, and watch it settle back into its dream.

choices.text: Remember it never opened its eyes

effects.log: That is how far there is still to climb. You will remember it every time you want to give up.

choices.text: Crawl out before it moves again

effects.log: Slowly, on elbows, through the water. You make it to the stair.

choices.text: Laugh, painfully

effects.log: Beaten by a sleeping lizard. Somewhere in that great head, perhaps, something is amused too.

events.text: You go past the dragon the only way anyone could: along its own body, through the slow river of its coils, so close that its scales brush your sleeve. It breathes, and the current carries you. It breathes again, and you are on the far side of the throne court, out of its reach, your heart in your throat.

choices.text: Look back at it

effects.log: Asleep. Huge, blue, patient. It did not even know you were there. Or it let you go.

choices.text: Keep going without a sound

effects.log: Not one sound until the stair. Then you sit down and shake.

choices.text: Touch one scale as you pass, for luck

effects.log: Cold as deep water. You will tell this story to grandchildren that are not born yet.

events.text: Halfway through the coils the dragon stirs in its sleep and its tail sweeps the court. It is not an attack. It does not need to be. You are thrown back the way you came, tumbling through the water, and fetch up on the stair you started from, the pearl as far away as the moon.

choices.text: Try to remember where the tail began to move

effects.log: Next time, if there is one, you will know where not to be.

choices.text: Rest on the stair and breathe

effects.log: You are alive, which, near a dragon, is a victory of a kind.

choices.text: Go back up while you still can

effects.log: Wise, perhaps. It feels like cowardice for a while.

events.text: You do not fight it. You sit down on the tiles in front of its face and breathe the way it breathes, slow, in and out, for a very long time, and at the end of it the dragon opens one great eye and lowers its head until its chin rests on the tiles beside you. The pearl rolls out from under it, to your knee. It is being given, not taken.

choices.text: Lay your hand on its nose

effects.log: It is cold and smooth and alive. It breathes out, and the whole palace sighs.

choices.text: Promise to come back

effects.log: A dragon's memory is long. You think it will hold you to it.

choices.text: Ask it, quietly, whether it wants to be free

effects.log: It closes its eye. You do not know if that is an answer.

events.text: You sit in front of the dragon and breathe with it, and for a long time you think it is working. Then it opens its eye, looks at you with something like pity, and blows out one breath that rolls you across the court and up against the wall. It is not ready to be anyone's. Perhaps it never will be.

choices.text: Accept it, and bow

effects.log: You bow from where you lie. It closes its eye. You are, at least, not food.

choices.text: Try to understand what you did wrong

effects.log: Your breath was a little too eager. A dragon can tell the difference between peace and wanting.

choices.text: Get up and leave with what dignity you have

effects.log: Not much. Enough.

events.text: The dragon's nostrils flare as you come near. It is smelling you, and something in what it smells makes its eye come open, slow and deep. It knows you. Not this face, not this body: something underneath that came down to this court in another life. It looks at you for a long time, as if trying to decide whether it is glad.

choices.text: Say: "I came back"

effects.log: Its eye closes slowly, then opens again. You choose to believe that means welcome.

choices.text: Ask it what you did last time

effects.log: It does not answer. But its tail curls a little away from you, which is something.

choices.text: Hold still and let it remember you

effects.log: It breathes you in for a full hour. When it is done, the water around you is warm.

events.text: You have stood in this court before and not walked out of it. You remember it now, all at once: the tail, the water, the slow dark. This time is different. This time you are still breathing, with the dragon behind you and the stair ahead. The old fear goes through you once, top to bottom, and then it is just a memory.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: It goes. You feel lighter by a whole life.

choices.text: Turn and look at the dragon, unafraid

effects.log: It is only a dragon. A very large one. You are only alive. That will do.

choices.text: Kneel and thank whatever kept you alive

effects.log: Luck, skill, the dragon's mood. You thank all of them.
