events.text: Your rival reached the throne court first and is already in the coils, slipping between them toward the pearl. Then the dragon stirs, and the coils begin to close. Your rival sees it too late. You are close enough to do something, or to do nothing.

choices.text: Pull your rival out of the coils

effects.log: You haul your rival clear just as they close. Neither of you says thank you. Neither needs to.

choices.text: Use the moment to get to the pearl first

effects.log: The coils hold your rival, and the way is open for you. A cold choice. It works.

choices.text: Shout a warning and nothing more

effects.log: Your rival twists free, barely. A debt, now, whether either of you likes it.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: You go to the dragon with Ga-ram's lullaby in the water around you, full and slow on new strings, and you breathe in its time. The dragon's eye opens, and in it you see the song: six hundred years of it, every night. It knows her. It has been listening the whole time. When it lowers its head to you, it is listening still.

choices.text: Hum the lullaby back to it

effects.log: It shuts its eye, content. Far above, Ga-ram plays on, and you think she can hear you.

choices.text: Tell it she is tired

effects.log: The dragon's breath goes out, long and slow, and the whole palace seems to think about it.

choices.text: Take the pearl gently and go

effects.log: It lets you. A gift from a dragon who has been sung to sleep by a friend for six centuries.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: The fight wakes the dragon fully, and for a terrible moment the whole palace shakes. Then, through the water, comes the lullaby: Ga-ram, playing harder than you have ever heard her, slow and stubborn. The dragon's eye grows heavy. It sinks back into its coils, and the pearl rolls out from under its chin as it sleeps.

choices.text: Go back and thank her first

effects.log: She is playing with bleeding fingers and does not look up. "Go," she says. "Before I stop."

choices.text: Take the pearl and go

effects.log: You owe the pearl to a dragon and the dragon's sleep to a ghost. It is a heavy thing to carry.

choices.text: Swear you will never wake it again

effects.log: The lullaby falters, just once, as if she heard you.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: It goes wrong at the dragon, and as you scramble back up the stair the lullaby rises around you: Ga-ram, playing faster, then slower, coaxing the great beast down. By the time you reach her hall it is asleep again. She does not stop. "You were lucky," she says. "It likes the third verse."

choices.text: Ask her to teach you the third verse

effects.log: She does, without missing a note. You will hum it for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Sit by her until your hands stop shaking

effects.log: She plays for you, and the palace goes very quiet.

choices.text: Thank her for your life

effects.log: "Everyone who goes down that stair is mine to keep alive," she says. "I lose most of them. Not you."

events.text: Pyo Seol-ah is at your shoulder when the pearl rolls free, and she does not reach for it. Her hands are shaking. "One touch," she says. "That is all. I have my master's cold in a bottle, here. If I touch the bottle to the pearl, the cold comes out. Please."

choices.text: Hold the pearl out to her

effects.log: She touches the bottle to it, and frost blooms on the glass and is gone. She is crying, under the water, where nobody can tell.

choices.text: Make her promise a debt first

effects.log: She promises without hesitating: one service, any service, from the Clear Tide Sect. Then the touch.

choices.text: Tell her no

effects.log: She looks at you for a long time. Then she nods and swims away, and the bead's light goes with her.

events.text: It goes wrong at the dragon, and it is Pyo Seol-ah who dives for you while the coils are still moving, loops the bead's cord around your wrist and kicks for the stair. She gets you there. She is gasping, half drowned herself. "That was the one breath I had," she says, "and you owe it to me."

choices.text: Swear to repay it

effects.log: She grins, weakly. "Good. I will think of something terrible."

choices.text: Ask whether she will try for the pearl now

effects.log: "Alone?" She laughs. "No. I will go home and sit by my master. That is all I can do now."

choices.text: Give her your own spirit stone for her master

effects.log: She stares at it. "That will buy him a month," she says. "A month is a great deal."

events.arc: The King Who Bound the Dragon
events.text: There, on the dragon's foreleg, is the other end of the golden chain: a cuff of gold sunk into the scales so long that they have grown over it. The dragon watches you as you come near it. It knows what you are looking at. It holds very still, the way a hurt animal holds still for the one who might help it.

choices.text: Cut the chain

effects.log: It takes everything you have, and a long time. When the last link parts, the dragon lifts its head, slowly, and looks up.

choices.text: Leave the chain as it is

effects.log: The dragon's eye closes. It has been disappointed for six hundred years; once more is nothing.

choices.text: Loosen the cuff, but do not cut it

effects.log: The scales under it are raw. You loosen it a finger's width. The dragon breathes out, long and slow.

events.arc: The King Who Bound the Dragon
events.text: It goes wrong at the dragon, and as you crawl away you see it: the chain. The golden cuff on its foreleg, the links running off into the dark toward the throne hall. The dragon's eye is on you, and on your hand, which is a finger's length from the nearest link.

choices.text: Cut it now, hurt as you are

effects.log: You hack at it with the last of your strength. It parts. The dragon goes very, very still.

choices.text: Crawl away; you can barely stand

effects.log: The dragon watches you go. You will think about that chain for a long time.

choices.text: Promise the dragon you will come back for it

effects.log: It closes its eye. It has heard that before, perhaps. From a king.

events.text: The way out is up: the whirlpool runs backwards when the realm begins to close, and it takes everyone left in the palace with it, spinning, up through green and then gold, until you break the surface of Lake Mireu into wind and sunlight and a sky so big it hurts.

choices.text: Float on your back and look at the sky

effects.log: Clouds. Birds. No ceiling of water. You lie there until a boat comes.

choices.text: Help the nearest swimmer to the shore

effects.log: A junior from a small sect, coughing up half the lake. You get the child to the reeds.

choices.text: Swim for the shore before the others

effects.log: You are on the bank, wringing out your sleeves, before most of them surface.

events.text: From the shore Lake Mireu looks like any other lake: wind, reeds, a heron. Nobody would guess that a whole court is standing bowed at the bottom of it, or that a dragon is sleeping under its tower. The fishermen on the bank do not look at the entrants coming out of the water. They have seen it before, every sixty years.

choices.text: Ask a fisherman what the lake was like before

effects.log: "Same," he says. "Always the same. My grandfather saw the last ones come out." He offers you a fish.

choices.text: Look back at the water for a long time

effects.log: Somewhere under it the music goes on. You think you can almost hear it.

choices.text: Walk away and do not look back

effects.log: The heron watches you go.

events.text: On the shore you hand the dragon pearl to the senior of {sr_sect}'s party. It goes into a box lined with silk and sealed with the sect's mark, and the senior looks at you with new eyes. Several masked faces on the far bank watch the box go into the senior's pack and turn away.

choices.text: Ask to carry the box home yourself

effects.log: The senior hesitates, then agrees. You walk back with a dragon's heart on your back.

choices.text: Say only that the dragon gave it freely

effects.log: The senior writes that down. The sect will tell the story for a generation.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on the masked faces

effects.log: One of them limps. One of them has a scar across the knuckles. You will know them again.

events.text: You come up out of the lake with {sr_sect}'s party and nothing in your hands, and stand dripping on the shore while the senior counts heads. One short. Then the whirlpool spits out the last of them, choking, and the count is whole, and the whole party sits down in the reeds at once.

choices.text: Sit with them and laugh

effects.log: Wet, empty-handed, all alive. It is the best moment of the expedition.

choices.text: Help the senior with the count, twice

effects.log: The senior notices. Next time, perhaps, your name goes on the senior's list.

choices.text: Promise yourself the next realm will not leave you empty

effects.log: Promises made on a lakeshore have a way of being kept.

events.text: The dragon pearl is inside your robe, warm against your skin, pulsing slow as a sleeping heart. You walk out of the reeds with your face blank. On the far bank, a dozen people who came out of the lake with nothing are very carefully not looking at you.

choices.text: Stay in the crowd all the way to the road

effects.log: Too many witnesses for anyone to try. You reach the town before dark.

choices.text: Hold the pearl a moment and listen to it

effects.log: It is breathing, very faintly. You feel your own breath slow to match.

choices.text: Hide it in your boot

effects.log: Undignified, and safe.

events.text: They were waiting in the reeds, masked, four of them, and they wanted the pearl. They did not get it. You come out of the shallows with the lake running off you, the pearl still warm against your skin, and four people running away very fast through the reeds.

choices.text: Let them run

effects.log: Four people who will think twice before waiting in reeds again.

choices.text: Catch the slowest and see the face

effects.log: A disciple of a sect that smiled at you on the way in. You let the disciple go, and remember.

choices.text: Tell the story at the nearest inn

effects.log: By morning it is a better story than the truth. Your name goes with it.

events.text: They were waiting in the reeds, and whatever they came for, you have nothing of it now. You sit on the shore of Lake Mireu in the evening light, bruised and dripping and empty-handed, and watch a heron fish where the whirlpool was. Sixty years until it opens again.

choices.text: Laugh at the heron, and at yourself

effects.log: It catches a fish. You catch nothing. You are both alive.

choices.text: Remember every voice you heard

effects.log: Two voices, behind masks. You will know them again.

choices.text: Swear an oath on the lake

effects.log: The next time something is taken from you, it will cost them. The lake hears.

events.text: You do not ride the whirlpool up with the others. You go back the way the cooks' well goes, up through the black stone and out into a farmer's yard three miles from the lake, where nobody is waiting for anyone. The farmer looks up from his cabbages, unsurprised, and goes on weeding.

choices.text: Help him weed a row before you go

effects.log: He thanks you with a cup of water. Best water you ever drank.

choices.text: Watch the lake from his hill

effects.log: Masked figures in the reeds, waiting for people who will never come out there. You smile.

choices.text: Go straight home by the back roads

effects.log: Quiet is its own reward.

events.text: You have come up out of this lake before. Your body knows the spin of the whirlpool running backwards and the exact moment to kick for the light. Somewhere in the soul something marks it down: again. The palace will still be there, and the dragon, and the music, the next time the realm opens.

choices.text: Promise to come back in the next life

effects.log: A promise to someone who is you and is not. It feels right.

choices.text: Promise to let the palace rest

effects.log: Some places should only be entered once or twice. The soul accepts this.

choices.text: Hold the memory as tightly as you can

effects.log: A soul keeps what it holds hardest. You hold the eye of the dragon.

events.text: A life of yours went down into this lake and never came up. This one does. You break the surface and the air goes into you all the way down, and you float there in the sunlight while something that has waited lifetimes for this breath lets go, slowly, like a held hand.

choices.text: Say goodbye to that life

effects.log: You do not know its name. You say it anyway, to the water.

choices.text: Thank it for the fear it left in your lungs

effects.log: That fear kept you alive down there. That other life paid for it.

choices.text: Swim to shore without a word

effects.log: There is nothing to say to the drowned except that you breathed. You have.

events.text: Word comes up the whirlpool before you do: somebody faced the sleeping dragon and came away with the pearl. On the shore people stand aside for you, and an old fisherman who has watched the lake for sixty years takes off his hat. Somebody is already making a song of it, badly.

choices.text: Correct the song

effects.log: The singer is grateful. The new verse is better, and your name scans.

choices.text: Say the dragon was kind

effects.log: Nobody believes it. The modesty does more for your name than the boast would have.

choices.text: Bow to the fisherman

effects.log: He bows back. Sixty years, and he never saw anyone come up with a pearl before.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: Before the whirlpool turns you go back to Ga-ram's hall one last time. She is playing, as always. "He knows I am tired now," she says. "You told him." Her fingers are almost transparent on the new strings. "Will you play the last verse for me? Only once. I would like to hear it from the outside."

choices.text: Play it for her

effects.log: Your hands are clumsy, the song is right. She listens with her eyes closed, and when you finish she is gone, and the zither plays on by itself, softly.

choices.text: Promise to send a real musician next opening

effects.log: She smiles. "Sixty years," she says. "I have waited longer." She plays you all the way to the whirlpool.

choices.text: Carry the zither out with her in it

effects.log: It is heavy and wet, and the music stops when you lift it. Up on the shore, in the sunlight, one string sounds by itself.

events.arc: The Last Song Under the Lake
events.text: You stop at Ga-ram's hall on your way out. She is still playing; she will always be playing. "Thank you," she says, without looking up. "For the strings, or the company. I forget which. Six hundred years does that." The whirlpool is turning. She lifts one hand from the strings, just for a moment, to wave.

choices.text: Wave back, and go

effects.log: The lullaby follows you all the way up into the sunlight. You will hear it in your sleep for years.

choices.text: Promise she will not be forgotten up above

effects.log: You keep it. A song goes around the teahouses a year later, about a musician under a lake. You started it.

choices.text: Stay one more verse

effects.log: You nearly miss the whirlpool. You do not regret it.

events.text: On the shore Pyo Seol-ah stands with the bottle of her master's cold in her hands, empty now, frost gone from the glass. "He will live," she says, as if she cannot quite believe it. "I owe you more than air." Her sect's party is waiting further up the bank. She does not go to them yet.

choices.text: Tell her she owes you nothing

effects.log: She shakes her head. "That is not how it works." A year later a gift arrives from the Clear Tide Sect. It is a breathing bead.

choices.text: Ask her to visit when her master is well

effects.log: She laughs. "He will want to thank you himself. He is very boring. I am sorry in advance."

choices.text: Say goodbye and walk away first

effects.log: You feel her watching you all the way up the bank.

events.text: On the shore Pyo Seol-ah wrings out her blue sleeves and looks at the lake, not at you. "My master will be dead by spring," she says, flatly. "I knew it was a long chance." Then she does look at you, and it is not a kind look, and it is not only for the pearl.

choices.text: Give her silver for medicine

effects.log: She takes it without a word. It may buy him a season. It does not buy her forgiveness.

choices.text: Say you are sorry

effects.log: "No," she says, "you are not." She walks to her sect's party and does not look back.

choices.text: Say nothing

effects.log: Some silences are an answer. She hears yours.

events.arc: The King Who Bound the Dragon
events.text: As the whirlpool turns to carry you up, the lake moves: a great slow surge from the bottom, and something vast and blue rising through the water past you, past the palace roofs, toward the light. On the throne, far below, the coral king lets his hand fall from his lap. You think, though you are much too far to see, that he is smiling.

choices.text: Watch the dragon break the surface

effects.log: It goes up out of Lake Mireu into the sky in a column of spray, and the fishermen on the bank fall to their knees. It rains for three days, warm.

choices.text: Go back down to the king

effects.log: He is coral, all of him, still and at rest. You close his eyes. The palace will sleep now.

choices.text: Pray the dragon is glad, not angry

effects.log: Three days of rain, all over the province, warm and gentle. Glad, then. Somewhere, a drought ends.

events.arc: The King Who Bound the Dragon
events.text: The whirlpool turns, and as it carries you up you hear him again, far below, patient and calling: "Is anyone there? Anyone at all?" The chain still holds. The dragon still sleeps. The king will be calling when the realm opens again in sixty years, and sixty after that.

choices.text: Call down that you heard him

effects.log: The calling stops, for a moment. Then it starts again, softer.

choices.text: Tell yourself it was the right choice

effects.log: A province of farms above that lake. The dragon chained, the hills dry. Perhaps it was. You will wonder.

choices.text: Promise to come back and cut it, next life

effects.log: A promise to someone who is you and is not. The soul writes it down.

events.text: The barrier gives way like a curtain of warm rain, and the smell hits you: a thousand herbs at once, sweet and bitter and green, so strong it makes your eyes water. {sr_realm} lies below you, terrace on terrace of overgrown gardens running down into white mist, and the flowers nearest the path turn their heads, slowly, to look at you.

choices.text: Breathe it in deeply

effects.log: Your head swims, then clears. Every channel in your body feels rinsed.

choices.text: Cover your nose and mouth with a damp cloth

effects.log: Wise. The juniors who breathed deep are sitting down already, dizzy and giggling.

choices.text: Bow to the flowers that are watching

effects.log: They turn away again, satisfied. You feel a little foolish and a little welcome.

events.text: The first rule of the Herb Valley is written on a stone at the gate, in a hand so old it is half moss: LOW MIST HEALS. HIGH MIST KEEPS. Everyone reads it. Nobody is quite sure what "keeps" means. Somewhere above, on the high meadows, you can see shapes lying very still in the grass.

choices.text: Promise yourself to stay low

effects.log: You keep to the lower terraces all day. The mist there takes the ache out of old bruises.

choices.text: Climb a little way to see the shapes

effects.log: Entrants from some past opening, asleep in the high grass, peaceful and untouched. You come back down very quickly.

choices.text: Copy the writing on the stone

effects.log: An old physician's hand. Reading it twice, you find a second line beneath the first, almost worn away: AND THE SERPENT KEEPS ME.

events.text: The party from {sr_sect} has come with baskets, not weapons, at least on the outside. The senior in charge hands out a list: twelve herbs, their leaves drawn in ink, and at the bottom, underlined twice, the thousand-year ginseng. "The rest is for the pharmacy," the senior says. "That last one is for the sect master. Do not come back and tell me you tried."

choices.text: Promise to fill the whole list

effects.log: The senior looks doubtful, and writes your name at the top.

choices.text: Ask what the ginseng is for

effects.log: "Ask the sect master," the senior says, which means the senior does not know either.

choices.text: Study the drawings until you know every leaf

effects.log: By the time the barrier opens you could pick them blind.

events.text: The crack in the barrier is under the roots of a great old tree on the valley's rim, and you go through it on your belly among the roots and the beetles. On the far side the roots go on, down into the valley, as if the tree had been trying for a thousand years to reach the garden below and was nearly there.

choices.text: Follow the roots down

effects.log: They lead you by a path no party knows, under ferns taller than you, to the second terrace.

choices.text: Rest a moment in the tree's shade

effects.log: The roots are warm, like something alive. You come out of the rest stronger than you went in.

choices.text: Mark the tree for your way out

effects.log: A knot of grass tied around a root. You will be glad of it later.

events.text: You have read about the great realms all your life, and none of the books said the flowers would sing. They do: a high, thin humming from the bell-shaped ones by the path, rising and falling as the wind moves them. It is your first great realm, and you stand at its gate with your mouth open, and an old entrant laughs at you, not unkindly.

choices.text: Ask the old entrant what the singing means

effects.log: "It means they are happy," the old one says. "When they stop, run." Good advice.

choices.text: Hum back to them

effects.log: A few of them seem to turn toward you. It is probably the wind. You do not think it is the wind.

choices.text: Pick one, to keep

effects.log: It stops singing the moment it leaves the stem. You carry it all day anyway, feeling guilty.

events.text: You know this path. Not this life: some other one, with other hands, that walked here and knew which leaves to pick. Your fingers go to a patch of low grey moss by the gate without your telling them, and pinch off a tip, and put it in your mouth, and the taste is the taste of a memory. Bitter, and then sweet.

choices.text: Trust your hands and let them gather

effects.log: They fill a pouch with herbs you do not know the names of. Every one is worth something.

choices.text: Stop and try to remember that life

effects.log: A garden of your own. A cough in the house. Someone you were trying to save. You do not get the ending.

choices.text: Spit it out and walk on

effects.log: You are not that person. But the taste stays all day.

events.text: High above the gate, on the meadows where the mist keeps what it takes, you can see where a past life of yours lay down and did not get up. You do not know how you know. You only look at a patch of grass among the sleepers there, and your whole body says: there. That was you.

choices.text: Promise that life you will stay low

effects.log: You will. Every step, today, you will feel it watching you keep the promise.

choices.text: Climb up to the place, carefully, holding your breath

effects.log: Nothing is there but grass that grows a little greener. You touch it, and come down shaking.

choices.text: Turn your back on the meadow

effects.log: Some deaths are better left in the grass where they happened.

events.text: After enough realms you stop being dazzled and start being useful. The juniors at the gate are staring at the singing flowers. You are looking at the soil, the slope, the way the mist moves, and reading the valley like a page of a physician's notebook: where the herbs will be thickest, and where the ground will hold a snake.

choices.text: Tell the juniors where not to step

effects.log: Two of them are about to put their feet on the sleeping vine. They step back. They will live to be veterans.

choices.text: Go straight for the richest terrace

effects.log: You have a full pouch by noon.

choices.text: Teach one junior to read the slope

effects.log: It costs an hour. The junior listens like a disciple.

events.text: The young ones at the gate look at your grey hair and wonder what you are doing here. You know exactly what you are doing here. Half the herbs in this valley are for old age, and the other half are for young fools who eat the wrong ones. You have been both. You know which is which.

choices.text: Brew yourself a tea of low-terrace leaves

effects.log: It takes the stiffness out of your knees for the first time in years.

choices.text: Warn a young fool off the wrong berries

effects.log: The young fool sulks, and lives.

choices.text: Go in first, slow and sure

effects.log: Slow and sure gets you to the third terrace before the young ones have stopped arguing.

events.text: Underneath the flowers' singing there is another sound, too low to hear with your ears: something very large breathing, deep in the valley, under the mist. The others do not seem to feel it. You feel it in your teeth. Whatever guards the ginseng is so far beyond you that its breath alone makes you dizzy.

choices.text: Sit and breathe until the dizziness passes

effects.log: It does, slowly. Something in your channels settles to a deeper rhythm than before.

choices.text: Chew a low-terrace leaf for courage

effects.log: It tastes like grass and gives you nothing but the feeling of having done something. That is enough.

choices.text: Promise yourself you will only look at the guardian, not fight it

effects.log: A sensible vow. It sits easier in you than bravery would.

events.text: Your rival is already inside the gate, kneeling in a bed of red herbs and picking with both hands, and looks up at you with a grin and a full basket. "You are late," your rival says. "Everything worth taking by the gate is already mine."

choices.text: Say the gate was never where the good herbs grow

effects.log: The grin fades a little. You walk past into the mist, and hear the basket being put down.

choices.text: Snatch a handful from the basket as you pass

ok.log: You are three steps away with a fistful of red herbs before your rival can stand up.

fail.log: A hand closes on your wrist. You leave with nothing and a bruise.

choices.text: Kneel down and pick beside your rival

effects.log: You pick in silence, side by side, for an hour. It is almost companionable.

events.text: At the mouth of the valley an old man sits in a garden chair that has grown into the ground, and so has he: from the knees down he is root, sunk deep in the soil, and there are leaves in his white hair. "Visitors," he says, delighted. "I am Bae. I planted all this. Would you do an old gardener a kindness?"

choices.text: Ask what kindness

effects.log: "Seeds," he says, and holds out a pouch. "For the high terrace, where my first garden was. I cannot walk there any more."

choices.text: Ask him about the guardian

effects.log: His face changes. "Old Green," he says. "I raised her from an egg. She is only guarding what I asked her to. Please, do not kill her."

choices.text: Tell him you have no time

effects.log: He nods, as if he expected it. "Nobody does, in here," he says. "That is the joke of the place."

events.text: By the stream that runs down the valley a young woman in the green-and-black robes of the Hundred Grass Hall is pouring dark powder into the water from a paper twist. She sees you and does not stop. "The serpent drinks from this stream," she says. "By tonight she will be slow. By tomorrow she will be easy. I am Gal Mi-reu. Want to share the ginseng?"

choices.text: Knock the paper out of her hand

effects.log: The rest of the powder goes into the moss. She stares at you with real hatred. "Do you know what that cost?"

choices.text: Agree to share

effects.log: She smiles, quick and thin. "Good. I do not like doing all the work." She tucks the empty paper away.

choices.text: Say nothing and walk on

effects.log: She shrugs and goes on pouring. Downstream, the singing flowers by the water go quiet.

events.text: A child is watching you from behind a fern taller than a house: a small, round-faced child in a coat made of green leaves, with bare feet the colour of washed roots. When you look, it giggles and hides. When you walk, it follows, a few steps behind, always just out of reach. No other entrant seems to see it.

choices.text: Hold out a rice cake

effects.log: It creeps closer, snatches the cake, and eats it in one bite. Then it sits beside you as if you were old friends.

choices.text: Ask its name

effects.log: "Sam-i," it says, in a voice like wind in leaves, and giggles again, and follows you down the path.

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: It follows you anyway, all morning, humming with the flowers.

events.text: The way down runs through the old terraces, where somebody once grew medicine in neat rows. The rows are gone now, a thousand years of wild growth over them, but here and there a stone marker still stands with a name cut into it: a herb, and under it, in a smaller hand, the name of a sick person it was meant for.

choices.text: Read the names as you pass

effects.log: Hundreds of them. A whole town, once. You wonder whether the herbs came in time.

choices.text: Gather from the rows that still grow true

effects.log: The old rows are the best of the valley. Your pouch grows heavy.

choices.text: Straighten a fallen marker

effects.log: A child's name, and a fever herb. You set it upright and wedge it with a stone.

events.text: Rain falls in the Herb Valley the way it falls nowhere else: warm, slow, and green, so thick with the smell of herbs that drinking it is like drinking medicine. Every entrant on the road stops and tips their face up to it. For a while, nobody is racing anybody.

choices.text: Drink it, as much as you can

effects.log: Your old injuries ache, then ease, then stop.

choices.text: Sit out the rain under a broad leaf with strangers

effects.log: Three sects under one leaf, sharing dried fruit. It will not last. It is good while it does.

choices.text: Use the quiet to cover ground

effects.log: Everyone else is standing still. You are two terraces further on when it stops.

events.text: The safe road goes through the physician's old walled garden, and every party in the realm is on it, picking. At the far gate a rival sect has posted two guards with spears. "The garden beyond is ours," one says. "We got here first. Go round."

choices.text: Go through anyway

ok.log: They look at you, and at each other, and step aside.

fail.log: They do not step aside. You go round after all, with a bruise for your trouble.

choices.text: Go round, as they say

effects.log: The long way round passes a bed of rare blue herbs nobody else noticed. Lucky.

choices.text: Offer them a trade of herbs to pass

effects.log: They take a handful of your best leaves and lift their spears.

events.text: On the safe road you meet a young entrant from some tiny sect sitting by the path, sweating, grey in the face. Bitten by something in the grass, the young one says, or ate the wrong leaf. Nobody else has stopped. The parties are going past with their eyes on the ginseng, far below.

choices.text: Stop and treat the young one

effects.log: An hour of work with low-terrace herbs, and the colour comes back. You will not get that hour back. You do not want it.

choices.text: Give the young one your water and go on

effects.log: Not much. More than anyone else gave.

choices.text: Go on with the others

effects.log: You look back once. The young one is still sitting there.

events.text: The beast road goes through the gorge of the stone bees, insects as big as your thumb that live in the cliffs and make honey from the valley's flowers. The honey is worth its weight in silver. The bees know that, and dislike anyone who knows it too.

choices.text: Take a comb from the lowest nest

ok.log: You are out of the gorge with a honeycomb in your shirt before the swarm has finished waking.

fail.log: They wake faster than you expected. You get away with honey on your hands and stings all over them.

choices.text: Smoke them with green leaves first

effects.log: The old way. They go drowsy and slow. You take a small comb and leave the rest.

choices.text: Leave the bees alone

effects.log: They hum along beside you all the way through the gorge, curious and polite.

events.text: Halfway along the beast road a spirit boar steps out of the ferns: shoulder-high, tusks of old ivory, moss on its back like a coat. It has been eating the valley's herbs for three hundred years, and it is very strong and very bad-tempered, and it is standing on the path.

choices.text: Stand your ground and stare it down

ok.log: It snorts, paws the ground, and goes back into the ferns. You do not let your knees shake until it is gone.

fail.log: It charges. You get out of the way, mostly.

choices.text: Throw it the herbs from your pouch

effects.log: It eats them happily and ignores you. Expensive, but whole.

choices.text: Back away slowly and find another path

effects.log: The other path is longer and full of thorns. You arrive scratched and alive.

events.text: The hidden road is a narrow path behind the waterfall that no other entrant sees, and you walk it as if you had walked it yesterday. Under an overhang at its end is a cache: a clay jar sealed with wax, and on the seal a mark you still make when you mean to come back. Inside, wrapped in oiled leaves, are herbs that have kept a whole lifetime.

choices.text: Take them, and leave the jar for next time

effects.log: You reseal it with wax from your own candle. Your future self will find it empty, and smile.

choices.text: Take half and leave half

effects.log: For whoever comes next, which will also be you. It feels fair.

choices.text: Sit behind the waterfall and remember

effects.log: Pieces come: a basket, a song, cold hands. Not enough for a story, but enough.

events.text: The hidden path goes past the high meadow where a past life of yours lay down in the keeping mist. From here, behind the waterfall, you can see the place, and the mist moving over it. You could walk out there and look. You know, with a certainty in your bones, that the mist would keep you too.

choices.text: Stay behind the waterfall

effects.log: You watch the mist for a long time and do not move. The life that lay down there would have wanted you to stay.

choices.text: Throw a flower out into the mist, for that life

effects.log: It falls into the grass and is still. You feel you have paid something.

choices.text: Turn away and walk on

effects.log: Not every grave is yours to visit.

events.text: The high mist comes down the valley on a wind, and the strong ones hold their breath and run, and you cannot run fast enough. You drop into a hollow under a ledge with your face in the wet earth and breathe through a cloth while the mist goes over, slow and white, a hand above your head.

choices.text: Count your breaths until it passes

effects.log: Two hundred and eleven. The mist moves on. You are still awake.

choices.text: Look up at it, once

effects.log: For one moment you understand why the sleepers on the meadow look so peaceful. Then you look down again, quickly.

choices.text: Pull a stranger into the hollow with you

effects.log: A junior from some small sect, slow as you are. You both live.

events.text: On a cliff path above the gorge you find a spirit herb growing out of the rock, a rare one, three leaves of blue fire, and your rival finds it at the same moment from the other side. The path is too narrow for two. The herb is too high to reach without someone holding someone else's ankle.

choices.text: Hold your rival's ankle and split the herb

effects.log: Your rival climbs, and picks it, and hands you half. It is the strangest moment of your rivalry.

choices.text: Race your rival for it

ok.log: You get there first, by a finger. Your rival's face is worth more than the herb.

fail.log: Your rival gets there first, and waves it at you from the far ledge.

choices.text: Let your rival have it

effects.log: A strange courtesy. Your rival stares after you, suspicious.

events.text: The high terrace where Bae's first garden grew is bare earth now, in a ring of old stones. You sow his seeds there as he told you, one in each hand-width, and before you have finished the last row the first are already up: green shoots, then leaves, then small white flowers, opening all at once, as if the soil had been waiting a thousand years for exactly this.

choices.text: Sit and watch them grow

effects.log: In an hour the terrace is a garden again. Down at the valley mouth, very faintly, you think you hear an old man laugh.

choices.text: Take one flower to bring back to him

effects.log: It stays fresh in your hand all day.

choices.text: Keep a few seeds back for yourself

effects.log: He said all of them. You keep five. They are warm in your pocket.

events.text: Bae's voice reaches you on the road, carried somehow through the roots under your feet. "Her name is Old Green," he says. "She likes the song I used to sing when I watered the garden. Like this." He hums it: four notes, up and down. "If you must face her, hum that. She may remember me."

choices.text: Learn the four notes

effects.log: You hum them all the way down the valley until they are part of your breath.

choices.text: Promise him again you will not kill her

effects.log: The roots under your feet seem to grip the ground a little tighter, gratefully.

choices.text: Ask why he asked her to guard the ginseng

effects.log: "So that nobody would take it before it was ready," he says. "A thousand years. I think it is ready now."

events.text: Gal Mi-reu follows you down the valley, sulking, a few steps behind. On the third terrace she stops you with a hand on your arm. "My hall will throw me out if I come back with nothing," she says. "My mother is in debt to it. Do you understand now? The poison was all I had."

choices.text: Offer to help her find another way

effects.log: She stares at you. "There is no other way." But she keeps walking beside you, not behind.

choices.text: Tell her that is not your problem

effects.log: "No," she says. "It never is." She drops back again, further this time.

choices.text: Share your herbs with her, enough to sell

effects.log: A pouch of good leaves. "This will pay one month," she says. "It is a start."

events.text: Downstream from Gal Mi-reu's poison, the valley is dying. The singing flowers by the water have stopped singing; their heads hang. A spirit deer is lying in the shallows, breathing hard, its eyes on you. Gal Mi-reu sees it too, and her face does not change, but she stops walking.

choices.text: Make her help you brew an antidote

effects.log: She knows the poison, so she knows the cure. It takes all afternoon. The deer gets up. So do the flowers, slowly.

choices.text: Keep going: the serpent will be weak

effects.log: She falls in beside you. Neither of you looks back at the deer.

choices.text: Treat the deer yourself, alone

effects.log: You do what you can. The deer lives. The stream does not get better.

events.text: Sam-i walks ahead of you now, showing the way: a spring where the water tastes of honey, a fallen log over a stream that nobody else would find, a bed of moss so soft you nearly sleep. Each time it stops it looks back to make sure you are still there. Its bare feet leave no prints. Where it stands, small green shoots come up.

choices.text: Ask it what it is

effects.log: It thinks about it seriously. "Old," it says at last. "Older than the gardener. I was the first thing he planted."

choices.text: Let it ride on your shoulders

effects.log: It weighs almost nothing and smells of earth after rain. It laughs the whole way down the terrace.

choices.text: Drink from its spring

effects.log: The water goes through you like warm light.

events.text: Whatever else you remember of the serpent, you will remember how quiet it was. A thousand years old, longer than a village street, moss growing in the gaps between its scales, and it moved through the ferns without a sound. Its eyes are the gold of old honey. They are not cruel. They are tired, the way a guard is tired at the end of a very long watch.

choices.text: Bow to it

effects.log: One long watchman to a short one. It lowers its head, a little.

choices.text: Remember how it moved

effects.log: Never quite where you looked, always where it meant to be. You will practise that for years.

choices.text: Look at the ginseng it guards

effects.log: A root like a sleeping child, glowing faintly gold under the ferns. You understand now why it is guarded.

events.text: When it is over the whole valley is hushed. The singing flowers have stopped, the bees are still, the mist hangs where it is. Then, from somewhere far up the terraces, one flower starts to hum again, and another, until the whole valley is singing as if nothing had happened.

choices.text: Listen to all of it

effects.log: You will hear that singing in your sleep for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Move on before the serpent stirs again

effects.log: Sensible. You are three terraces up before you stop to breathe.

choices.text: Pick a leaf from where you stood, to remember

effects.log: A plain green leaf. It will never wilt. You do not know why.

events.text: The serpent fights the way water fights: around you, under you, always moving. When it finally sinks down in the ferns it does not seem defeated so much as finished, as if it had only been waiting for someone strong enough. It looks at you, then at the ginseng, and closes its golden eyes.

choices.text: Leave it alive and take the ginseng

effects.log: Its breathing slows to sleep. You take the root gently. Behind you, the flowers start to sing again.

choices.text: Take the ginseng and one of its scales

effects.log: A moss-green scale, big as a plate. It does not stir. A fine thing to carry out.

choices.text: Sit with it a while before you go

effects.log: A thousand-year watch, ended. Someone should be there for it.

events.text: The serpent wraps you before you see it move, and squeezes, and lets go. That is all. You lie in the ferns unable to breathe, and it looks down at you with its old gold eyes, and goes back to its coils around the ginseng as if you had never come.

choices.text: Remember it let you go

effects.log: It could have kept squeezing. It did not. That will matter to you more than winning would have.

choices.text: Crawl to the low mist and let it heal you

effects.log: An hour in the low mist and you can breathe again. Most of you.

choices.text: Swear you will come back stronger

effects.log: The serpent does not care. You do.

events.text: You go past the serpent the way the mist goes: low, slow, without a sound, through the ferns along its back, so close that the moss on its scales brushes your hand. It does not turn its head. On the far side of the hollow you stand up, shaking, with the ginseng glowing behind you and the way to the gate open ahead.

choices.text: Look back once

effects.log: Its golden eye is open, watching you. It let you go. You are sure of it.

choices.text: Take a few herbs from beside it as you pass

effects.log: The ones nearest the ginseng are the best of the valley.

choices.text: Keep moving without a sound

effects.log: Not a sound until the next terrace. Then you laugh, and cannot stop.

events.text: Halfway through the ferns the serpent's tail moves, lazily, the way a sleeping cat's does, and you are flung out of the hollow into a bed of thorns. It does not follow. It does not need to. The ginseng glows on, out of reach, behind a thousand years of coils.

choices.text: Pick the thorns out and try to understand what you did

effects.log: You stepped on a fern that was singing. It told the serpent. Next time you will listen.

choices.text: Lie in the thorns and laugh

effects.log: It hurts. You laugh anyway.

choices.text: Go back up to the low mist and heal

effects.log: It takes an hour. You come out of it whole.

events.text: You kneel in front of the serpent with your hands open and empty and let it smell you, slowly, from head to foot. It takes a long time. At the end of it the great green head lowers to the ground beside you, and the coils around the ginseng loosen, one by one, like fingers opening.

choices.text: Lay your hand on its head

effects.log: Cool and dry and old. It breathes out, and the ferns around you shiver.

choices.text: Take the ginseng gently, and thank it

effects.log: It watches you lift the root. Its eyes close, as if a weight had gone out of it.

choices.text: Ask it if it wants to leave the valley

effects.log: It looks at you for a long time. Then it looks up the valley, toward the gate, and lies down again.

events.text: You kneel in front of the serpent with your hands open, and it smells you, and its eyes go cold. Something on you it does not like: the blood of beasts you killed on the road, or only the wanting in you. It hisses once, like a kettle, and the gust of it rolls you back across the hollow.

choices.text: Accept it and bow from where you lie

effects.log: It turns away. You are not worth fighting. That is its own kind of lesson.

choices.text: Think about what it smelled on you

effects.log: You know what it was. You will carry that thought out of the valley.

choices.text: Try once more, slower

effects.log: It hisses again, and this time you hear it: not now. Maybe not ever. You go.

events.text: The serpent's tongue flickers out, tasting the air around you, and stops. It tastes again. Something under this face and body it has met before: a soul that came down to this hollow in another life. Its golden eyes widen. You do not know if that life came as a friend or a thief. Neither, it seems, does the serpent.

choices.text: Hold still and let it decide

effects.log: It tastes you for a long time. Then it relaxes, just a little. Friend, then. Probably.

choices.text: Say: "I came back"

effects.log: Its head tilts, slowly. The coils around the ginseng shift.

choices.text: Ask it what you did last time

effects.log: It does not answer. But it does not strike either.

events.text: This is the hollow where some life of yours ended. You know it now, all at once: the ferns, the golden eyes, the coils closing. And this time you are still standing, with the serpent behind you and the whole valley singing. The old fear goes through you once, top to bottom, and then it is only a memory.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: It goes. You feel lighter by a whole life.

choices.text: Turn and look at the serpent, unafraid

effects.log: It looks back. Neither of you is the same as last time.

choices.text: Thank whatever kept you alive

effects.log: Luck, skill, the serpent's mercy. All three.

events.text: Your rival reached the hollow first and has the ginseng in both hands when the serpent wakes. The coils close. Your rival drops the root and fights, and is losing, and you are close enough to do something, or to wait for it to be over.

choices.text: Throw yourself at the coils

effects.log: The serpent lets your rival go to deal with you. You both get out. Neither of you mentions it again.

choices.text: Take the dropped root while the serpent is busy

effects.log: A cold choice. It works.

choices.text: Shout and draw the serpent's eye

effects.log: It turns. Your rival slips free. A debt now, owed whether either of you likes it.

events.text: You hum Bae's four notes, up and down, as the serpent rises over you, and it stops. Its golden eyes go wide and wet. It lowers its great head to yours and breathes you in, slowly, the way an old dog breathes in a coat that smells of someone it has not seen in a thousand years. Then it lies down across the path, and lets you by.

choices.text: Tell it Bae is still at the valley mouth

effects.log: Its head comes up. It looks toward the gate for a long time. Then it lies down again, its eyes on the path.

choices.text: Stroke its head and go on

effects.log: Cool, dry, very old. It closes its eyes.

choices.text: Sing it the whole song, not just the notes

effects.log: You only know four notes. You make up the rest. It does not seem to mind.

events.text: The serpent sinks down in the ferns, beaten, and lies there breathing hard, and you remember the old gardener at the valley mouth. "Please," he said, "do not kill her." Your weapon is still in your hand. Nobody is watching. She would not get up again for a long time.

choices.text: Let her live

effects.log: You step back. She watches you go with old gold eyes.

choices.text: Take a scale as proof, and leave her

effects.log: One green scale. She does not stir. You leave the rest of her in peace.

choices.text: Make sure she will not follow

effects.log: You do not kill her. But you make sure. It is not something you will tell the gardener.

events.text: It goes badly at the hollow, and the serpent has you in its coils, and then it stops. Its tongue flickers over your sleeve, over your hands. Seeds. The smell of Bae's seeds, still on your fingers from the high terrace. It lets you go, all at once, and lies in the ferns watching you, as if waiting for news.

choices.text: Tell it the garden is growing again

effects.log: Its eyes close slowly. When they open again it looks younger.

choices.text: Get out while you can

effects.log: You do. It does not follow.

choices.text: Leave a seed on the ground for it

effects.log: It curls around the seed as you go, the way it curls around the ginseng.

events.text: The serpent is sick. You see it the moment you reach the hollow: its scales dull, its golden eyes cloudy, its breath rattling. Gal Mi-reu's poison has done exactly what she said it would. Whatever happened at the hollow, it was not a fair fight, and Gal Mi-reu, beside you, will not look at the serpent at all.

choices.text: Tell her to brew the antidote now, for the serpent

effects.log: She stares at you. Then she does it, with shaking hands, and the serpent drinks. It will live.

choices.text: Take what you came for

effects.log: The serpent watches you go with cloudy eyes. Gal Mi-reu follows, silent.

choices.text: Ask her if this is what she wanted

effects.log: "I wanted my mother out of debt," she says. "This is what it costs." She does not look up.

events.text: Gal Mi-reu stands beside you at the hollow with her poison pouch shut and a staff in her hands, and when the serpent rises she does not run. She is better than you thought: quick, precise, every strike aimed to stun and not to kill. Whatever happens at the hollow, you are not alone in it.

choices.text: Thank her afterward

effects.log: "Do not," she says. "I only did it because the deer would have died." But she is smiling.

choices.text: Offer her a share of what you found

effects.log: She looks at it for a long time. "Half a share," she says. "For my mother. The rest is yours."

choices.text: Ask her why she changed her mind

effects.log: "I did not," she says. "You changed it for me. I am still angry about that."

events.text: At the hollow Sam-i runs ahead of you, straight to the serpent's head, and pats it on the nose. The serpent lowers its head to the child, gently. And the glow you saw from the terrace is not under the ferns at all: it is the child, faintly gold all over. "She guards me," Sam-i says. "I am what you came for. Did you not know?"

choices.text: Tell Sam-i you will not take it

effects.log: It considers this seriously. "Then I will give you my first root," it says. "That one I can spare." It does.

choices.text: Ask what happens if you take it

effects.log: "I sleep," it says. "In a box, in a house, until someone eats me. It is all right. It is what I am for." It looks at you.

choices.text: Kneel down to its height

effects.log: It puts a small root-hand on your face. It is warm.

events.text: It goes badly at the hollow, and the serpent has you, and then Sam-i is there, between you and the great head, both small arms spread wide. "Not this one," it says. "This one is my friend." The serpent stops. It looks at the child for a long time, and puts you down, and goes back to its coils.

choices.text: Thank Sam-i

effects.log: It giggles. "You are heavy," it says. "Like a stone. I like stones."

choices.text: Ask the child what it is

effects.log: "The first thing the gardener planted," it says. "She keeps me safe until I am ready."

choices.text: Lie still and breathe

effects.log: The child sits beside you, humming with the flowers, until you can stand.

events.text: The gate opens at the head of the valley like a curtain of warm rain being drawn back, and the entrants climb toward it, terrace by terrace, with their baskets and their bruises. Behind you the flowers are singing as if nobody had ever come. In sixty years they will still be singing.

choices.text: Turn and look back from the top terrace

effects.log: The whole valley, green and gold and white, singing under its mist. Then the gate closes on it.

choices.text: Help a limping stranger up the last terrace

effects.log: A junior from some tiny sect, half asleep from the wrong mist. You get the child through.

choices.text: Walk through with your eyes shut, breathing in

effects.log: The last breath of the valley goes all the way down. Then the plain air of the world, thin and cold.

events.text: Outside the barrier the world smells of nothing at all. After the valley it is like going deaf. People who went in with full voices come out whispering, and an old herbalist at the gate, who has waited sixty years to see this opening, sniffs each entrant as they pass and smiles at what is left on their clothes.

choices.text: Let the old herbalist sniff your sleeve

effects.log: "Low terrace," the old one says. "And bee honey, and fear." Accurate.

choices.text: Sit on a rock until your nose comes back

effects.log: It takes an hour. The world smells of dust and woodsmoke. It is good.

choices.text: Count who came out, and who did not

effects.log: Fewer than went in. Some are asleep on the high meadow now, peaceful, and will be for good.

events.text: At the gate you hand the thousand-year ginseng to the senior of {sr_sect}'s party. It goes into a box of cedar lined with damp moss, and the senior holds it like a newborn. Around the gate, a dozen masked faces see the box and turn away. Nobody comes near a sect's banner with that many witnesses.

choices.text: Ask what the sect master will use it for

effects.log: "Ask the sect master," the senior says, then, quietly: "It will buy the master twenty years." Twenty years of a sect master is a great deal.

choices.text: Say the serpent let you take it

effects.log: The senior writes that down. The sect will tell it for a generation.

choices.text: Watch the masked faces

effects.log: One has a herbalist's stained fingers. You will remember the stains.

events.text: You come out with {sr_sect}'s party and a basket of ordinary herbs, and the senior goes through it leaf by leaf at the gate, and nods. Not the ginseng. But the pharmacy will be full this winter, and nobody in the party fell asleep on the high meadow. The senior seems more relieved by that than by any root.

choices.text: Ask the senior about the last opening

effects.log: "I lost my best friend to the high mist," the senior says. "Sixty years ago. She is still up there, asleep." Nothing more.

choices.text: Promise the next realm will be different

effects.log: Promises made at a closing gate have a way of being kept.

choices.text: Be glad of a full basket

effects.log: A full basket and a full party. There are worse ways to leave a great realm.

events.text: The thousand-year ginseng is wrapped in damp moss inside your robe, warm as a sleeping animal, and you can smell it through the cloth: earth and honey and something older. So can everyone else at the gate. You keep your face still and walk.

choices.text: Stay in the thick of the crowd

effects.log: Too many eyes for anyone to try anything. You reach the road before dark.

choices.text: Rub mud on your robe to hide the scent

effects.log: Undignified, and it works. The masked ones at the gate sniff and look elsewhere.

choices.text: Hold your hand over it and feel it breathe

effects.log: It is breathing, very slowly. You feel your own breath deepen to match.

events.text: They were waiting in the ferns by the gate, masked, with herbalist's gloves and a net, and they wanted the ginseng. They did not get it. You come out through the barrier with your sleeve torn, your breath ragged, and the root still warm against your ribs, and three people running away through the ferns.

choices.text: Let them run

effects.log: Three people who will think twice before waiting in ferns again.

choices.text: Keep the net they dropped

effects.log: Good silk, and a sect's mark on the cord. Useful to know.

choices.text: Tell the story at the nearest inn

effects.log: By morning it is a better story than the truth. Your name goes with it.

events.text: They were waiting in the ferns by the gate, and whatever they came for, you have nothing of it now. You sit outside the barrier on a rock, bruised and empty-handed, with nothing but the smell of the valley still in your clothes. Sixty years until it opens again. The smell will be gone in a week.

choices.text: Breathe it in while it lasts

effects.log: Honey and earth and green rain. For a week, it is enough.

choices.text: Remember the gloves they wore

effects.log: Herbalist's gloves, stained the colour of one sect's dyes. You will know them again.

choices.text: Swear an oath on the valley

effects.log: Next time something is taken from you, it will cost them. The flowers, very faintly, hum.

events.text: You do not take the gate. You go back up the valley to the great tree on the rim, and out the way the roots go, on your belly among the beetles, into the plain air of the world. Nobody is waiting at the tree. Nobody saw you come or go. The valley closes behind you with a sigh like wind in leaves.

choices.text: Sit under the tree and rest

effects.log: Its roots are warm. You sleep an hour, and dream of singing flowers.

choices.text: Watch the gate from the ridge

effects.log: Masked figures in the ferns, waiting for you. You smile, and go the other way.

choices.text: Untie your knot of grass from the root

effects.log: You leave a fresh one, for the next opening.

events.text: You have come out of this valley before. Your body knows the drop in the smell at the gate, the sudden thin air of the world, the way the sky looks too big. Something in the soul marks it down: again. The flowers will be singing when the realm opens next, and the serpent will be waiting.

choices.text: Promise to come back in the next life

effects.log: A promise to someone who is you and is not. It feels right.

choices.text: Promise to let the valley rest

effects.log: Some gardens are better left to grow. The soul accepts this.

choices.text: Hold the memory as hard as you can

effects.log: A soul keeps what it holds tightest. You hold the singing.

events.text: A life of yours went into this valley and lay down on the high meadow and never came out. This one does. At the gate you stop and breathe the plain air of the world, all the way down, and something that has been asleep a very long time stirs in you and lets go, gently, like a hand opening.

choices.text: Say goodbye to that life

effects.log: You do not know its name. You say goodbye anyway, to the mist.

choices.text: Thank it for the warning it left you

effects.log: Every time the high mist moved today, you knew. That other life paid for it.

choices.text: Walk on without a word

effects.log: There is nothing to say to the sleeping except that you woke. You have.

events.text: Word reaches the gate before you do: somebody faced the thousand-year serpent and came away with the ginseng. The old herbalist at the gate bows to you, very low, and three young herbalists from three sects ask, all at once, how. Somebody is already making a song of it.

choices.text: Tell them how, honestly

effects.log: It is less heroic than the song. They write it all down anyway.

choices.text: Say the serpent was kind

effects.log: Nobody believes it. The modesty spreads further than the boast would.

choices.text: Bow back to the old herbalist

effects.log: Sixty years of waiting at that gate. The old one has never seen this before.

events.text: On your way to the gate you stop at the valley mouth. Bae is sitting in his root-chair, his face turned up the valley, and there are new leaves in his hair. "She is all right," he says, before you can speak. "I can feel her through the roots. Thank you." He holds out his hand. In it is a single seed, brown and warm.

choices.text: Take the seed and plant it in the world

effects.log: You plant it by your own door. It grows into a small tree that never gets sick, and neither, quite, do you.

choices.text: Ask him to come out with you

effects.log: He laughs. "My legs are a thousand years deep," he says. "And she would miss me." He waves you on.

choices.text: Sit with him a while before the gate

effects.log: He tells you about the Grey Fever, and the town, and the first garden. You nearly miss the gate. You do not regret it.

events.text: At the valley mouth Bae is sitting very still in his root-chair, his face turned up the valley, listening to something only he can hear. He does not look at you as you pass. "Go on," he says, quietly. "The gate will not wait. Nothing in here ever does, except her."

choices.text: Tell him what happened at the hollow

effects.log: He listens with his eyes closed. When you finish he nods. "She is old," he says. "So am I." Nothing more.

choices.text: Leave him a cup of water from the low spring

effects.log: His roots drink it before you have stepped away.

choices.text: Walk past without a word

effects.log: Some debts are too heavy to talk about at a gate.

events.text: At the gate Gal Mi-reu stops and looks back at the valley, where the stream runs clear again and the flowers by the water are singing. "My hall will call me a fool," she says. "I am going to tell them I chose to be one." Then, not looking at you: "If they throw me out, I am coming to find you. You owe me a job."

choices.text: Tell her she will have one

effects.log: She snorts. "You say that now." A year later she knocks, and you keep your word.

choices.text: Give her silver toward her mother's debt

effects.log: She takes it stiffly. "This is a loan," she says. It is not.

choices.text: Tell her she was never a fool

effects.log: She looks at you, sharp and surprised, and then away. "Go on," she says. "Before I poison you."

events.text: At the gate Gal Mi-reu walks out beside you, quick and quiet, and the stream behind you is still dark, and the flowers by the water are still silent. She will be welcome at her hall. She does not look happy about it. "Do not tell anyone how," she says. "And I will not tell anyone you watched."

choices.text: Agree, and go your own way

effects.log: A pact of silence. It weighs more than any herb you carried out.

choices.text: Tell her you will carry an antidote back next opening

effects.log: She laughs, harshly. "Sixty years. The stream will heal before then." She is probably right.

choices.text: Tell her the hall will not make her happy

effects.log: "No," she says. "But it will make my mother free." She walks away.

events.text: Sam-i walks you to the gate, holding your hand, and stops just short of the barrier. Its little face is solemn. "You will not remember me properly," it says. "Nobody does. That is all right. Plant the root I gave you somewhere warm. Then I will be in two places." It lets go of your hand.

choices.text: Plant its root by your door

effects.log: It grows into a small, stubborn plant that flowers gold every spring. Children who play near it never seem to fall ill.

choices.text: Promise to remember it properly

effects.log: You do. For the rest of your life, you remember a child in a coat of leaves, and you are kinder for it.

choices.text: Pick it up and hug it goodbye

effects.log: It weighs almost nothing and smells of rain. It laughs. Then it is a pile of leaves in your arms, and then it is gone.

events.text: Sam-i follows you to the gate but does not come close. It stands in the ferns with its arms folded, watching you go, and the gold glow on it is very faint now. You are not sure what you did, or did not do, at the hollow. The child is. It lifts one hand, slowly, and waves.

choices.text: Wave back

effects.log: It smiles, a small sad smile, and is only leaves.

choices.text: Go back and kneel by it

effects.log: It lets you. It puts a leaf in your hand. The leaf never wilts.

choices.text: Walk through the gate without looking back

effects.log: You feel it watching you all the way into the plain air of the world.
